### Create `apps/api/src/activity/flows.ts`

```ts
import {
  ACTIVITY_NEWER_CAP,
  ACTIVITY_PAGE_SIZE,
  decodeActivityCursor,
  encodeActivityCursor,
  type ActivityEntry,
  type ActivityKind,
  type ActivityNewerQuery,
  type ActivityNewerResponse,
  type ActivityNotShown,
  type ActivityPage,
  type ActivityPlace,
  type ActivityQuery,
  type ActivitySettings,
} from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { ModerationActivityEntry, ModerationForActivity } from "../moderation";
import { enforceWriteLimit, type EngagementAction, type SocialForActivity } from "../social";
import type { ActivityRepo, ReceivedRow } from "./repo";

/** The codes this module raises itself; the social module's limits raise rate_limited and service_unavailable. */
export type ActivityErrorKind = "invalid_request";

/** An expected, user-facing failure, which the app's error handler renders as an ErrorEnvelope. */
export class ActivityError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: ActivityErrorKind,
    readonly status: 400,
    message = "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ActivityError";
  }
}

export interface ActivityDeps {
  repo: ActivityRepo;
  /** The social module's interface: the views of an entry's post and of a follow group's accounts. */
  social: SocialForActivity;
  /** The moderation module's interface: the entries of 5.5.2. Without it the list holds the social entries only. */
  moderation?: ModerationForActivity;
  /** The store every per-account limit counts in, through the social module's enforceWriteLimit. */
  limits: RateLimitStore;
  log: Logger;
  now: () => Date;
  /** Entries a page holds: ACTIVITY_PAGE_SIZE, which a test may lower to page through few entries. */
  pageSize: number;
}

/** A place in the list: an entry's time and key. Keys compare code unit by code unit, as the repository's "C" collation does. */
type Placed = { at: string; key: string };

/** Newest first: the later time, then the higher key. Times are ISO text to the microsecond, which sorts as it reads. */
const newestFirst = (a: Placed, b: Placed): number => (a.at !== b.at ? (a.at < b.at ? 1 : -1) : a.key < b.key ? 1 : a.key > b.key ? -1 : 0);

/**
 * Counts one write of the account under its bucket (9.5). These limits do not depend on the account's age (tiers.ts), so
 * the account's creation time is not read: the clock's time stands in for it.
 */
async function limit(deps: ActivityDeps, viewer: string, action: EngagementAction): Promise<void> {
  const now = deps.now();
  await enforceWriteLimit(deps.limits, viewer, action, now, now);
}

/** A row of the merged list before its view: a social row of the repository or a moderation entry. */
type Merged = ({ source: "social" } & Awaited<ReturnType<ActivityRepo["list"]>>[number]) | ({ source: "moderation" } & ModerationActivityEntry);

/**
 * GET /api/activity (5.5): one page for the signed-in account, newest first by (at, key). The stored seen marker is read
 * first, as the request finds it. The social rows (5.5.1) and, on the tab All, the moderation entries (5.5.2) are each
 * asked for one more than a page before the cursor; their union is sorted by (at, key), the page is the first
 * ACTIVITY_PAGE_SIZE, and the next cursor is made from its last row when the union held more. Then the views: each post
 * entry's PostView through the social module (loadPostViews, so postAccess decides), each follow group's Authors; an entry
 * whose view does not come back, which only a race between the query and the views can cause, is dropped from the page
 * (the cursor still stands after it). Each entry is `new` when its time is later than the stored marker.
 */
export async function activityPage(deps: ActivityDeps, viewer: string, query: ActivityQuery): Promise<ActivityPage> {
  const place: ActivityPlace | null = query.cursor === undefined ? null : decodeActivityCursor(query.cursor);
  if (query.cursor !== undefined && place === null) throw new ActivityError("invalid_request", 400, "That page of Activity does not exist.");
  const seenAt = await deps.repo.seenAt(viewer);
  const wanted = deps.pageSize + 1;
  const [social, moderation] = await Promise.all([
    deps.repo.list(viewer, query.tab, place, wanted),
    query.tab === "all" && deps.moderation ? deps.moderation.authorActivity(viewer, place, wanted) : Promise.resolve([]),
  ]);
  const merged: Merged[] = [...social.map((row) => ({ source: "social" as const, ...row })), ...moderation.map((row) => ({ source: "moderation" as const, ...row }))].sort(newestFirst);
  const page = merged.slice(0, deps.pageSize);
  const last = page.at(-1);
  const nextCursor = merged.length > deps.pageSize && last ? encodeActivityCursor({ at: last.at, key: last.key }) : null;

  const postIds = page.flatMap((row) => (row.source === "social" && row.type === "post" ? [row.postId] : []));
  const actorIds = [...new Set(page.flatMap((row) => (row.source === "social" && row.type === "follows" ? row.actorIds : [])))];
  const [views, authors] = await Promise.all([postIds.length > 0 ? deps.social.postViews(viewer, postIds) : new Map(), actorIds.length > 0 ? deps.social.authors(actorIds) : new Map()]);
  const isNew = (at: string) => seenAt === null || at > seenAt;
  const items: ActivityEntry[] = page.flatMap((row): ActivityEntry[] => {
    if (row.source === "moderation") {
      const { source: _source, ...entry } = row;
      return [{ ...entry, new: isNew(row.at) }];
    }
    if (row.type === "post") {
      const post = views.get(row.postId);
      return post ? [{ type: "post", kind: row.kind, key: row.key, at: row.at, new: isNew(row.at), post }] : [];
    }
    const actors = row.actorIds.flatMap((id) => (authors.has(id) ? [authors.get(id)!] : []));
    return actors.length > 0 ? [{ type: "follows", key: row.key, at: row.at, new: isNew(row.at), count: row.count, actors }] : [];
  });
  return { items, nextCursor, seenAt };
}

/**
 * GET /api/activity/newer (5.8): how many entries are newer than `since` (every entry without it), under the list's own
 * rules and counted as the list draws them (a day of follows is one), up to ACTIVITY_NEWER_CAP. On the tab All the
 * moderation entries count too, asked for the newest ACTIVITY_NEWER_CAP. No route counts unread entries for anything
 * else (decision 4): this one is asked only by the open Activity screen, about times it already shows.
 */
export async function newerCount(deps: ActivityDeps, viewer: string, query: ActivityNewerQuery): Promise<ActivityNewerResponse> {
  const since = query.since ?? null;
  const [social, moderation] = await Promise.all([
    deps.repo.newer(viewer, query.tab, since, ACTIVITY_NEWER_CAP),
    query.tab === "all" && deps.moderation ? deps.moderation.authorActivity(viewer, null, ACTIVITY_NEWER_CAP) : Promise.resolve([]),
  ]);
  const newerModeration = moderation.filter((entry) => since === null || entry.at > since).length;
  return { count: Math.min(ACTIVITY_NEWER_CAP, social + newerModeration) };
}

/** POST /api/activity/seen (5.7): counted under activity-seen, then the marker moves forward, never past the clock. */
export async function markSeen(deps: ActivityDeps, viewer: string, at: string): Promise<void> {
  await limit(deps, viewer, "activity-seen");
  await deps.repo.markSeen(viewer, at);
}

/** GET /api/activity/settings: the account's rules, the defaults when it never changed them. */
export async function readSettings(deps: ActivityDeps, viewer: string): Promise<ActivitySettings> {
  return deps.repo.settings(viewer);
}

/** PUT /api/activity/settings (5.2): counted under activity-settings, then stored; they apply to new acts only. */
export async function saveSettings(deps: ActivityDeps, viewer: string, settings: ActivitySettings): Promise<ActivitySettings> {
  await limit(deps, viewer, "activity-settings");
  return deps.repo.saveSettings(viewer, settings);
}

/** One received entry as the export writes it (11.2). */
export interface ReceivedEntry {
  kind: ActivityKind;
  at: string;
  postId: string | null;
  actorHandle: string;
  shown: true | ActivityNotShown;
}

/** The account's Activity as the export holds it: the marker, the rules, and every entry it received, read in pages. */
export interface ActivityExport {
  seenAt: string | null;
  settings: ActivitySettings;
  received: AsyncIterable<ReceivedEntry[]>;
}

/**
 * Why the list does not show a received entry, or true (11.2). When several rules hide it, the first of these wins: the
 * actor's account is deleted (`actor_deleted`); for an entry about a post, the post is not visible or a block stands
 * between the two accounts either way (`post_not_visible`: the post is then hidden from this account, so a row hidden only
 * by a block, which a mention can leave behind in 5.6's race, says that and names no post); for a follow, the follow is
 * gone (`unfollowed`; a block removes it); then the account's own mute (`muted`). A post the account may not see is
 * named by no id, whatever reason wins, so the export never discloses another person's moderation.
 */
export function receivedEntry(row: ReceivedRow): ReceivedEntry {
  const aboutPost = row.postId !== null;
  const postHidden = aboutPost && (!row.postVisible || row.blocked);
  const shown: true | ActivityNotShown = row.actorDeleted
    ? "actor_deleted"
    : postHidden
      ? "post_not_visible"
      : !aboutPost && (!row.followStands || row.blocked)
        ? "unfollowed"
        : row.muted
          ? "muted"
          : true;
  return { kind: row.kind, at: row.at, postId: postHidden ? null : row.postId, actorHandle: row.actorHandle, shown };
}

/**
 * The export's member (11.2): the marker and the rules read at once, and every received entry newest first, ungrouped,
 * read in keyset pages of `pageSize` as the export writes them, so a long list is never whole in memory.
 */
export async function exportEntries(deps: ActivityDeps, userId: string, pageSize: number): Promise<ActivityExport> {
  const [seenAt, settings] = await Promise.all([deps.repo.seenAt(userId), deps.repo.settings(userId)]);
  return {
    seenAt,
    settings,
    received: {
      async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
        let after: { at: string; id: string } | null = null;
        for (;;) {
          const rows: ReceivedRow[] = await deps.repo.received(userId, after, pageSize);
          if (rows.length > 0) yield rows.map(receivedEntry);
          if (rows.length < pageSize) return;
          const last = rows.at(-1)!;
          after = { at: last.at, id: last.id };
        }
      },
    },
  };
}

/** Entries a page of Activity holds unless a test says otherwise. */
export const DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = ACTIVITY_PAGE_SIZE;
```

### Create `apps/api/src/activity/index.ts`

```ts
/**
 * The only file outside `src/activity/` may import. Everything else in the module is private and the architecture test
 * fails the build if another file reaches into it.
 *
 * The activity module (2d design, sections 5 and 9.1): the one screen that tells a person what others did with them and
 * what korbat told them about their own content. It reads activity_items and activity_state (the social module writes
 * the entries, in the act's transaction), the posts' views and the follow groups' accounts through the social module's
 * interface, and the moderation entries through the moderation module's (`authorActivity`); it writes nothing but the
 * seen marker, the rules and the retention's deletes. No route of it counts unread entries for anything but the open
 * screen (decision 4), and no staff route reads it: the staff and moderation modules never import it.
 */
import { ActivityNewerQuery, ActivityQuery, ActivitySettings, SeenRequest } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Hono, type Context, type MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import type { JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import { validate } from "../lib/validate";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { ModerationForActivity } from "../moderation";
import type { SocialForActivity } from "../social";
import { DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE, activityPage, exportEntries, markSeen, newerCount, readSettings, saveSettings, type ActivityDeps, type ActivityExport } from "./flows";
import { createActivityRepo } from "./repo";
import { createRetentionJob } from "./retention";

export { ActivityError } from "./flows";
export type { ActivityErrorKind, ActivityExport, ReceivedEntry } from "./flows";

/** What the account module needs from this one (11.2): the export's member, its received entries read in pages of `pageSize`. */
export interface ActivityForAccount {
  exportEntries(userId: string, pageSize?: number): Promise<ActivityExport>;
}

export interface CreateActivityOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The social module's interface for this one: social.forActivity. */
  social: SocialForActivity;
  /** The moderation module's interface for this one: moderation.forActivity. Without it the list holds no moderation entry. */
  moderation?: ModerationForActivity;
  /** The store every per-account limit counts in, as the social module's. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account, with CSRF and Origin checked for its writes. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;
  /** Entries a page holds; ACTIVITY_PAGE_SIZE unless a test lowers it to page through few entries. */
  pageSize?: number;
}

/** Rows a page of the export reads at a time unless a test says otherwise, as the social module's lists. */
const EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE = 1_000;

/** The routes of 9.2, mounted at /api/activity, every one behind the session; the app's error handler renders their refusals. */
function activityRoutes(deps: ActivityDeps, guard: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>) {
  const r = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  const me = (c: Context<AppEnv>): string => c.get("session")!.userId;
  r.get("/", guard, validate("query", ActivityQuery), async (c) => c.json(await activityPage(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/newer", guard, validate("query", ActivityNewerQuery), async (c) => c.json(await newerCount(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  // Only what the account reads: open to a suspended account (9.4).
  r.post("/seen", guard, validate("json", SeenRequest), async (c) => {
    await markSeen(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("json").at);
    return c.body(null, 204);
  });
  r.get("/settings", guard, async (c) => c.json(await readSettings(deps, me(c))));
  r.put("/settings", guard, validate("json", ActivitySettings), async (c) => c.json(await saveSettings(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("json"))));
  return r;
}

export function createActivity(options: CreateActivityOptions) {
  const deps: ActivityDeps = {
    repo: createActivityRepo(options.apiDb),
    social: options.social,
    moderation: options.moderation,
    limits: options.rateLimitStore,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
    pageSize: options.pageSize ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE,
  };
  const forAccount: ActivityForAccount = {
    exportEntries: (userId, pageSize = EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE) => exportEntries(deps, userId, pageSize),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    /** GET /, GET /newer, POST /seen, GET and PUT /settings, which app.ts mounts at /api/activity. */
    routes: activityRoutes(deps, options.requireSession),
    /** The interface the account module's export uses. */
    forAccount,
    /**
     * Starts activity-retention under the jobs' shared lock: a round every hour, the first an hour after the start. Returns
     * the function that stops it; a round in flight finishes.
     */
    startRetention: (lock: JobLock) => createRetentionJob(deps, lock).start(),
  };
}

export type Activity = ReturnType<typeof createActivity>;
```

### Create `apps/api/src/activity/repo.ts`

```ts
import { sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import { ACTIVITY_DEFAULTS, ACTIVITY_KEEP_DAYS, type ActivityPlace, type ActivitySettings, type ActivityTab } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";

/**
 * The activity module's statements (2d design, sections 5.5 to 5.7, 5.10 and 11.2), through the korbat_api pool. It reads
 * activity_items and activity_state, and the social tables an entry is judged by (the actor's profile, blocks, mutes,
 * follows and the post's state); it writes nothing but activity_state and the retention's deletes. The entries
 * themselves are written by the social module, in the act's transaction.
 *
 * Every time is the database's, written to the microsecond (ActivityTime), so the list's order, the cursor, the newer
 * count and the seen marker compare times of one clock exactly. Keys compare as text in the "C" collation, code unit by
 * code unit, which is how the flow's TypeScript compares them too, so a cursor means the same place to both.
 */

/** A timestamptz expression as ISO text in UTC with its microseconds. The expression is written here, never input. */
const micros = (expression: string): SQL => sql.raw(`to_char(${expression} at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')`);

/** One row of the list before its views: an entry about a post, or a UTC day's follows with the newest three followers. */
export type ActivityRow =
  | { type: "post"; key: string; at: string; kind: "reply" | "mention" | "quote"; postId: string }
  | { type: "follows"; key: string; at: string; count: number; actorIds: string[] };

/**
 * One received entry as the export reads it, ungrouped, with each of 5.5.1's rules answered on its own: whether the actor
 * is deleted, a block stands either way, the recipient mutes the actor, the post is visible, and the follow stands.
 */
export interface ReceivedRow {
  id: string;
  kind: "reply" | "mention" | "quote" | "follow";
  at: string;
  postId: string | null;
  actorHandle: string;
  actorDeleted: boolean;
  blocked: boolean;
  muted: boolean;
  postVisible: boolean;
  followStands: boolean;
}

/**
 * The rules of 5.5.1 as SQL over an entry `i` of `recipient`, each one fragment, written once for the list, the newer
 * count and the export: the actor is live, no block stands between the recipient and the actor in either direction, the
 * recipient does not mute the actor (social/repo.ts's otherWelcome: otherNotBlocked and the mute), a follow's follow
 * still stands, and a post's post is visible (social/repo.ts's visibleTo for a reader who is not its author, since the
 * recipient never wrote it). The views then pass each post through postAccess, as every read of a post does.
 */
const rules = (recipient: string) => ({
  actorLive: sql`exists (select 1 from profiles a where a.id = i.actor_id and a.deleted_at is null)`,
  noBlock: sql`not exists (select 1 from blocks b where (b.blocker_id = ${recipient}::uuid and b.blocked_id = i.actor_id) or (b.blocked_id = ${recipient}::uuid and b.blocker_id = i.actor_id))`,
  notMuted: sql`not exists (select 1 from mutes m where m.muter_id = ${recipient}::uuid and m.muted_id = i.actor_id)`,
  followStands: sql`(i.post_id is not null or exists (select 1 from follows f where f.follower_id = i.actor_id and f.followee_id = ${recipient}::uuid))`,
  postVisible: sql`(i.post_id is null or exists (select 1 from posts p where p.id = i.post_id and p.state = 'visible'))`,
});

/** All five: the entry is shown. */
function shownTo(recipient: string): SQL {
  const r = rules(recipient);
  return sql`${r.actorLive} and ${r.noBlock} and ${r.notMuted} and ${r.followStands} and ${r.postVisible}`;
}

/**
 * The entries of the list as the screen draws them (5.5.1), as one CTE `entries` with key, at, kind, post_id, count and
 * actors: an entry that is not a follow on its own (`e:` and its id, at its time), and the follows of each UTC day as one
 * entry (`f:` and the day, at the newest follow's time, the number of distinct followers and the three newest). A day is
 * a fixed bucket, so a group never splits across pages. Conversations keeps replies, mentions and quotes only.
 */
function entries(recipient: string, tab: ActivityTab): SQL {
  const kinds = tab === "conversations" ? sql`and i.kind::text <> 'follow'` : sql``;
  return sql`
    shown as (
      select i.id, i.kind::text as kind, i.actor_id, i.post_id, i.created_at from activity_items i
       where i.recipient_id = ${recipient}::uuid ${kinds} and ${shownTo(recipient)}
    ),
    entries as (
      select 'e:' || s.id::text as key, s.created_at as at, s.kind, s.post_id, 1 as count, null::uuid[] as actors
        from shown s where s.kind <> 'follow'
      union all
      select 'f:' || to_char(d.day, 'YYYY-MM-DD'), d.at, 'follow', null::uuid, d.count, d.actors
        from (select (s.created_at at time zone 'UTC')::date as day, max(s.created_at) as at, count(distinct s.actor_id)::int as count,
                     (array_agg(s.actor_id order by s.created_at desc, s.actor_id desc))[1:3] as actors
                from shown s where s.kind = 'follow' group by 1) d
    )`;
}

export function createActivityRepo(db: Db) {
  const rows = async <T>(query: SQL): Promise<T[]> => (await db.execute(query)) as unknown as T[];

  return {
    /** A page of the list, newest first by (at, key), after `before` when given, at most `limit` rows. */
    async list(recipient: string, tab: ActivityTab, before: ActivityPlace | null, limit: number): Promise<ActivityRow[]> {
      const raw = await rows<{ key: string; at: string; kind: string; post_id: string | null; count: number; actors: string[] | null }>(sql`
        with ${entries(recipient, tab)}
        select e.key, ${micros("e.at")} as at, e.kind, e.post_id, e.count, e.actors::text[] as actors from entries e
         where ${before === null ? sql`true` : sql`(e.at, e.key collate "C") < (${before.at}::timestamptz, ${before.key} collate "C")`}
         order by e.at desc, e.key collate "C" desc
         limit ${limit}::int`);
      return raw.map((row) =>
        row.kind === "follow"
          ? { type: "follows", key: row.key, at: row.at, count: row.count, actorIds: row.actors ?? [] }
          : { type: "post", key: row.key, at: row.at, kind: row.kind as "reply" | "mention" | "quote", postId: row.post_id! },
      );
    },

    /**
     * How many entries of the list are newer than `since` (every entry when null), counted as the list draws them (a day
     * of follows is one), and at most `cap`: the count stops there, so a busy account costs no more than a quiet one.
     */
    async newer(recipient: string, tab: ActivityTab, since: string | null, cap: number): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = await rows<{ n: number }>(sql`
        with ${entries(recipient, tab)}
        select count(*)::int as n from (select 1 from entries e where ${since === null ? sql`true` : sql`e.at > ${since}::timestamptz`} limit ${cap}::int) x`);
      return row?.n ?? 0;
    },

    /** The stored seen marker, null before the first visit. */
    async seenAt(recipient: string): Promise<string | null> {
      const [row] = await rows<{ seen_at: string | null }>(sql`select ${micros("seen_at")} as seen_at from activity_state where account_id = ${recipient}::uuid`);
      return row?.seen_at ?? null;
    },

    /**
     * Moves the marker to `at`, never back and never past the server's clock (5.7): the later of the stored marker and the
     * earlier of `at` and now(), so a marker older than what another device sent changes nothing. The row is made with the
     * defaults on the first visit; activity_state_guard holds the same two rules.
     */
    async markSeen(recipient: string, at: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.execute(sql`
        insert into activity_state (account_id, seen_at) values (${recipient}::uuid, least(${at}::timestamptz, now()))
        on conflict (account_id) do update set seen_at = greatest(activity_state.seen_at, least(${at}::timestamptz, now()))`);
    },

    /** The account's rules (5.2): its row, or ACTIVITY_DEFAULTS for an account that never changed them. */
    async settings(recipient: string): Promise<ActivitySettings> {
      const [row] = await rows<ActivitySettings>(sql`select replies::text as replies, mentions::text as mentions, quotes::text as quotes, follows from activity_state where account_id = ${recipient}::uuid`);
      return row ? { replies: row.replies, mentions: row.mentions, quotes: row.quotes, follows: row.follows } : { ...ACTIVITY_DEFAULTS };
    },

    /** Stores the four rules, upserting the row (its marker untouched), and answers them as stored. They apply to new acts only. */
    async saveSettings(recipient: string, settings: ActivitySettings): Promise<ActivitySettings> {
      const [row] = await rows<ActivitySettings>(sql`
        insert into activity_state (account_id, replies, mentions, quotes, follows)
        values (${recipient}::uuid, ${settings.replies}::activity_reach, ${settings.mentions}::activity_reach, ${settings.quotes}::activity_reach, ${settings.follows})
        on conflict (account_id) do update set replies = excluded.replies, mentions = excluded.mentions, quotes = excluded.quotes, follows = excluded.follows
        returning replies::text as replies, mentions::text as mentions, quotes::text as quotes, follows`);
      return { replies: row!.replies, mentions: row!.mentions, quotes: row!.quotes, follows: row!.follows };
    },

    /**
     * A page of every entry the account received that korbat still holds, newest first by (created_at, id), after `after`,
     * with the actor's handle now and each rule's answer, for the export (11.2): shown or not, ungrouped.
     */
    async received(recipient: string, after: { at: string; id: string } | null, limit: number): Promise<ReceivedRow[]> {
      const r = rules(recipient);
      const raw = await rows<{
        id: string;
        kind: ReceivedRow["kind"];
        at: string;
        post_id: string | null;
        actor_handle: string;
        actor_deleted: boolean;
        blocked: boolean;
        muted: boolean;
        post_visible: boolean;
        follow_stands: boolean;
      }>(sql`
        select i.id, i.kind::text as kind, ${micros("i.created_at")} as at, i.post_id, a.handle as actor_handle, a.deleted_at is not null as actor_deleted,
               not ${r.noBlock} as blocked, not ${r.notMuted} as muted, ${r.postVisible} as post_visible, ${r.followStands} as follow_stands
          from activity_items i join profiles a on a.id = i.actor_id
         where i.recipient_id = ${recipient}::uuid
           and ${after === null ? sql`true` : sql`(i.created_at, i.id) < (${after.at}::timestamptz, ${after.id}::uuid)`}
         order by i.created_at desc, i.id desc
         limit ${limit}::int`);
      return raw.map((row) => ({
        id: row.id,
        kind: row.kind,
        at: row.at,
        postId: row.post_id,
        actorHandle: row.actor_handle,
        actorDeleted: row.actor_deleted,
        blocked: row.blocked,
        muted: row.muted,
        postVisible: row.post_visible,
        followStands: row.follow_stands,
      }));
    },

    /**
     * The retention (5.10): deletes at most `batch` entries written more than ACTIVITY_KEEP_DAYS ago, by id, and answers
     * how many went. activity_items_created_brin finds the old rows; the time is the database's.
     */
    async deleteExpired(batch: number): Promise<number> {
      const gone = await rows<{ id: string }>(sql`
        delete from activity_items where id in (
          select id from activity_items where created_at < now() - make_interval(days => ${ACTIVITY_KEEP_DAYS}::int) order by id limit ${batch}::int)
        returning id`);
      return gone.length;
    },
  };
}

export type ActivityRepo = ReturnType<typeof createActivityRepo>;
```

### Create `apps/api/src/activity/retention.ts`

```ts
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { ActivityRepo } from "./repo";

/** The job's name: its rounds run under the shared lock job:activity-retention, and its log line carries it. */
export const RETENTION_JOB = "activity-retention";
/** A round every hour (5.10). */
export const RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS = 60 * 60_000;
/** How long the lock outlives a crash; a round is refreshed every half of it while it runs. */
const RETENTION_LOCK_MS = 15 * 60_000;
/** Entries one statement deletes (5.10), so no round holds a long lock on the table. */
export const RETENTION_BATCH = 5_000;

/**
 * The job activity-retention (2d design, sections 5.10 and 11.1; decision 11): under a Valkey lock, one instance at a time,
 * every hour, it deletes the entries written more than ACTIVITY_KEEP_DAYS ago, a batch at a time by id until a batch
 * comes back short, and logs only how many went, never an id, an account or a time. The seen marker, the rules and the
 * mentions have no retention of their own: they live as long as the account and its posts. `batch` is a test's to lower.
 */
export function createRetentionJob(deps: { repo: ActivityRepo; log: Logger }, lock: JobLock, batch: number = RETENTION_BATCH) {
  return createJob({
    name: RETENTION_JOB,
    intervalMs: RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS,
    lockTtlMs: RETENTION_LOCK_MS,
    lock,
    log: deps.log,
    run: async () => {
      let deleted = 0;
      for (;;) {
        const gone = await deps.repo.deleteExpired(batch);
        deleted += gone;
        if (gone < batch) break;
      }
      if (deleted > 0) deps.log.info({ job: RETENTION_JOB, deleted }, "activity: old entries deleted");
    },
  });
}
```

### Replace `apps/api/src/account/context.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { ActivityForAccount } from "../activity";
import type { AuthForAccount } from "../auth";
import type { ImportsForAccount } from "../imports";
import type { MediaForAccount } from "../media";
import type { ModerationForAccount } from "../moderation";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { SocialForAccount } from "../social";

/** The codes this module raises itself; the modules it calls raise their own, which the app's error handler also renders. */
export type AccountErrorKind = "not_found" | "invalid_request" | "rate_limited" | "service_unavailable";
export type AccountErrorStatus = 400 | 404 | 429 | 503;

const MESSAGES: Record<AccountErrorKind, string> = {
  not_found: "Not found.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  rate_limited: "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.",
  service_unavailable: "That could not be done right now. Try again in a moment.",
};

/** An expected, user-facing failure. The HTTP layer turns it into an ErrorEnvelope with this code and status. */
export class AccountError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: AccountErrorKind,
    readonly status: AccountErrorStatus,
    message: string = MESSAGES[code],
    /** Set for rate_limited and service_unavailable so the response can carry Retry-After. */
    readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "AccountError";
  }
}

export function accountErrorMessage(code: AccountErrorKind): string {
  return MESSAGES[code];
}

/**
 * The account module owns no table: it sequences the other three modules through the interfaces their
 * index files export (1b design, section 5). The limit store is the one every per-account limit uses.
 */
export interface AccountDeps {
  auth: AuthForAccount;
  social: SocialForAccount;
  media: MediaForAccount;
  /**
   * The purge's forgetting of a deleted account's reports, in the moderation module's tables (3c design, section 7.10),
   * the export's moderation member (section 7.11), and (3e, section 7.8) the take-down of the terminated accounts whose
   * termination is final, at the start of each purge round. The server always hands it over; a test of the other steps
   * may leave it out: the purge then skips those steps, and the export writes the member with two empty lists.
   */
  moderation?: ModerationForAccount;
  /**
   * 3b Task 6 (design, sections 4.7 and 11.2): the purge's step for the account's imports and import key, inside the social
   * purge's transaction, with their files after it; and the export's member `imports`. The server always hands it over; a
   * test of the other steps may leave it out: the purge then deletes no import row, and the export's member is empty.
   */
  imports?: ImportsForAccount;
  /**
   * 2d (design, section 11.2): the export's member `activity`, the account's seen marker, rules and received entries. The
   * server always hands it over; a test of the other members may leave it out, and the member is then the defaults with no
   * entry. The purge needs nothing of it: the social module's purge deletes the account's entries, marker and mentions.
   */
  activity?: ActivityForAccount;
  limits: RateLimitStore;
  log: Logger;
  now: () => Date;
}
```

### Replace `apps/api/src/account/flows/export.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { ACTIVITY_DEFAULTS, OrderNoticeFacts, OrderTexts, STANDING_RULES, type Platform } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { ActivityExport, ReceivedEntry } from "../../activity";
import type { AccountExport } from "../../auth";
import type { ImportRecord } from "../../imports";
import type { ModerationExport } from "../../moderation";
import type { ProfileExport } from "../../social";
import { AccountError, type AccountDeps } from "../context";
import type { OpenFile, ZipWriter } from "../zip";

/** One export a day (1b design, section 10). */
export const EXPORTS_PER_WINDOW = 1;
export const EXPORT_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

const exportLimitKey = (userId: string) => `export:${userId}`;

/** The entry an image has in the archive; export.json names it under the post's media. */
export function mediaEntry(id: string): string {
  return `media/${id}.webp`;
}

/** The download's name: the handle and the day, so several exports of one account sort by date. */
export function exportFilename(handle: string, now: Date): string {
  return `korbat-export-${handle}-${now.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}.zip`;
}

/**
 * What the archive is written from. The account's own facts, the profile and the moderation member are
 * read before the first byte; the profile's lists are read page by page while export.json is written,
 * and the images, each behind the media module's checked open, go first, so `missingMedia` is complete
 * by the time the JSON that lists it is written.
 */
export interface ExportPlan {
  exportedAt: Date;
  /** The handle of the session that asked for the export: the id the auth module lists each session under. */
  currentSession: string;
  account: AccountExport;
  profile: ProfileExport;
  /** The decisions about the account that it was told of and its own reports, as the moderation module hands them over (3c design, section 7.11). */
  moderation: ModerationExport;
  /** 3b Task 6 (design, section 11.2): the account's imports, newest first, as the imports module hands them over. */
  imports: ImportRecord[];
  /** 2d (design, section 11.2): the seen marker and the rules, read at once, and the received entries, read in pages. */
  activity: ActivityExport;
  images: { id: string; open: OpenFile }[];
  /** The images whose file the checked open refused or could not find, filled while the images are written. */
  missingMedia: string[];
}

/**
 * Counts one export of the account in the daily window and refuses once it is used up. Taken before
 * anything is built or streamed, so a stream that fails midway still counts; Retry-After says when the
 * window resets.
 */
export async function enforceExportLimit(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string): Promise<void> {
  let hit: { count: number; resetMs: number };
  try {
    hit = await deps.limits.hit(exportLimitKey(userId), EXPORT_WINDOW_MS);
  } catch {
    // Fails closed: an export that cannot be counted is not made, and the client is told to retry shortly.
    throw new AccountError("service_unavailable", 503, undefined, 30);
  }
  if (hit.count > EXPORTS_PER_WINDOW) throw new AccountError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, Math.max(1, Math.ceil(hit.resetMs / 1000)));
}

/**
 * Gives the day's export back after a failure before the archive's first byte (a pool timeout, a
 * restart): the owner received nothing, so the attempt must not use up the day. Best effort: when the
 * store cannot be reached, the export stays counted and a warning says so, which costs the owner a day
 * at worst.
 */
export async function giveBackExport(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string, log: Logger): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await deps.limits.release(exportLimitKey(userId));
  } catch (err) {
    log.warn({ err, userId }, "account export: the day's export could not be given back after a failure before the first byte");
  }
}

const iso = (at: Date): string => at.toISOString();
const isoOrNull = (at: Date | null): string | null => (at ? at.toISOString() : null);

/**
 * What an account module built without the moderation module writes: the member is part of the format, so it is always
 * there. Its reporting counts are empty over the standing rules' frame, the number the moderation module would read.
 */
const NO_MODERATION: ModerationExport = {
  decisions: [],
  reports: [],
  strikes: [],
  standing: [],
  replies: [],
  reporting: { frameDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays, days: [], marks: [], markedReports: 0 },
  uploads: [],
  releases: [],
};

/** What an account module built without the activity module writes: the member is part of the format, so it is always there. */
const NO_ACTIVITY: ActivityExport = {
  seenAt: null,
  settings: { ...ACTIVITY_DEFAULTS },
  received: {
    async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
      // No entry to list.
    },
  },
};

/**
 * Reads what is needed before the first byte: the account's facts, sessions, devices and events (one
 * read, bounded by the 90 days of events), the profile's own fields, the list of images, and the
 * moderation member (the decisions the account was told of and its own reports, both short lists). The
 * four modules are asked at once, so a read that fails costs the owner nothing: no byte was sent yet.
 * `currentSession` is the handle of the session asking, which marks its entry among the sessions.
 * `pageSize` is how many rows of each profile list are read at a time; tests lower it.
 */
export async function buildExport(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string, currentSession: string, now: Date, pageSize?: number): Promise<ExportPlan> {
  const [account, profile, images, moderation, imports, activity] = await Promise.all([
    deps.auth.exportAccount(userId),
    deps.social.exportProfile(userId, pageSize),
    deps.media.exportImages(userId),
    // The server always hands the moderation module over; a test of the other members may leave it out.
    deps.moderation ? deps.moderation.exportFor(userId) : NO_MODERATION,
    // 3b Task 6: and the imports module; without it the member is empty.
    deps.imports ? deps.imports.exportFor(userId) : Promise.resolve([]),
    // 2d (11.2): and the activity module; without it the member holds the defaults and no entry.
    deps.activity ? deps.activity.exportEntries(userId, pageSize) : Promise.resolve(NO_ACTIVITY),
  ]);
  return { exportedAt: now, currentSession, account, profile, moderation, imports, activity, images, missingMedia: [] };
}

/** A list member of export.json, read in pages and written one element at a time. */
class Paged<T> {
  constructor(
    readonly pages: AsyncIterable<readonly T[]>,
    readonly element: (row: T) => unknown,
  ) {}
}

/** An object member written member by member, so that one of its members may be a list read in pages (2d's `activity`). */
class Members {
  constructor(readonly members: [string, unknown][]) {}
}

/** An array already in memory, as one page. */
function inMemory<T>(rows: readonly T[], element: (row: T) => unknown): Paged<T> {
  return new Paged(
    (async function* () {
      yield rows;
    })(),
    element,
  );
}

/** Fragments are gathered into pieces of about this many UTF-16 units, at most 3 bytes each in UTF-8: well under 64 KiB. */
const PIECE_CHARS = 16 * 1024;

/**
 * export.json in pieces, written exactly as JSON.stringify(document, null, 2) writes the whole
 * document: member by member at the top level, and the lists element by element, each element
 * stringified on its own and indented to its depth (JSON.stringify's output holds line breaks only
 * between tokens; one inside a string is escaped, so indenting after every line break is exact). No list
 * is ever whole in memory: each is read page by page as it is written.
 */
export async function* exportJson(plan: ExportPlan): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  let buffer = "";
  for await (const fragment of documentFragments(plan)) {
    buffer += fragment;
    if (buffer.length >= PIECE_CHARS) {
      yield buffer;
      buffer = "";
    }
  }
  if (buffer.length > 0) yield buffer;
}

async function* documentFragments(plan: ExportPlan): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  const { account, profile } = plan;
  const ref = (row: { postId: string; at: Date }) => ({ postId: row.postId, at: iso(row.at) });
  const other = (row: { handle: string; since: Date }) => ({ handle: row.handle, since: iso(row.since) });
  // The members in the order of the format (ExportFormat in the contracts); the order is part of the bytes.
  const members: [string, unknown][] = [
    ["format", "korbat-export-1"],
    ["exportedAt", iso(plan.exportedAt)],
    [
      "account",
      {
        id: account.account.id,
        email: account.account.email,
        createdAt: iso(account.account.createdAt),
        role: account.account.role,
        mfaEnabled: account.account.mfaEnabled,
        hasPassword: account.account.hasPassword,
        verified: account.account.verified,
        termsVersion: account.account.termsVersion,
        termsAcceptedAt: isoOrNull(account.account.termsAcceptedAt),
        // Inside the account, where the format places them; at most the cap of ten, so they are written with the account's other facts rather than paged.
        passkeys: account.passkeys.map((passkey) => ({ name: passkey.name, createdAt: iso(passkey.createdAt), lastUsedAt: isoOrNull(passkey.lastUsedAt), synced: passkey.synced, createdOn: passkey.createdOn })),
      },
    ],
    [
      "profile",
      {
        handle: profile.profile.handle,
        displayName: profile.profile.displayName,
        bio: profile.profile.bio,
        createdAt: iso(profile.profile.createdAt),
        handleHistory: [...profile.profile.handleHistory],
        // Last in the profile, where the format added it (2c); the member order is part of the bytes.
        showInExplore: profile.profile.showInExplore,
        // After it, where 3e added it (W.8): the retired handles of the history, with when.
        retiredHandles: profile.profile.retiredHandles.map((retired) => ({ handle: retired.handle, retiredAt: iso(retired.retiredAt) })),
        // 2d (11.2): the link-preview switch, last in the profile for now.
        sharePreviews: profile.profile.sharePreviews,
      },
    ],
    [
      "posts",
      new Paged(profile.posts, (post) => ({
        id: post.id,
        body: post.body,
        createdAt: iso(post.createdAt),
        replyToId: post.replyToId,
        quoteOfId: post.quoteOfId,
        state: post.state,
        deletedAt: isoOrNull(post.deletedAt),
        media: post.media.map((image) => ({ id: image.id, file: mediaEntry(image.id), altText: image.altText, width: image.width, height: image.height })),
        // 3b (11.2): after the images, where the format added it; null on a native post and on a tombstone.
        imported: post.imported === null ? null : { source: post.imported.source, originalCreatedAt: iso(post.imported.originalCreatedAt), shortened: post.imported.shortened },
        // 2d (11.2): last, the handles its stored mentions name as written, in text order, and its hidden-counts switch.
        mentions: [...post.mentions],
        countsHidden: post.countsHidden,
      })),
    ],
    ["likes", new Paged(profile.likes, ref)],
    ["reposts", new Paged(profile.reposts, ref)],
    ["bookmarks", new Paged(profile.bookmarks, ref)],
    ["following", new Paged(profile.following, other)],
    ["blocks", new Paged(profile.blocks, other)],
    ["mutes", new Paged(profile.mutes, other)],
    [
      "sessions",
      inMemory(account.sessions, (session) => ({ id: session.id, createdAt: iso(session.createdAt), lastUsedAt: iso(session.lastUsedAt), current: session.id === plan.currentSession })),
    ],
    [
      "devices",
      // The platform column is text; sign-in only ever writes one of the contract's three values.
      inMemory(account.devices, (device) => ({ label: device.label, platform: device.platform as Platform, firstSeenAt: iso(device.firstSeenAt), lastSeenAt: iso(device.lastSeenAt) })),
    ],
    ["events", inMemory(account.events, (event) => ({ type: event.type, at: iso(event.at) }))],
    // Complete by now: the images were written before the JSON.
    ["missingMedia", inMemory(plan.missingMedia, (id) => id)],
    // Where the format added it (3c). Each entry is written member by member in the format's order, so the bytes
    // do not depend on how the moderation module builds its objects, and nothing beyond the format is ever written.
    ["moderation", moderationMember(plan.moderation)],
    // 3b Task 6 (11.2): the account's imports, newest first, member by member in the format's order.
    [
      "imports",
      plan.imports.map((entry) => ({
        id: entry.id,
        source: entry.source,
        status: entry.status,
        createdAt: iso(entry.createdAt),
        endedAt: isoOrNull(entry.endedAt),
        statedAt: isoOrNull(entry.statedAt),
        choice:
          entry.choice === null
            ? null
            : { from: entry.choice.from, to: entry.choice.to, replies: entry.choice.replies, warnings: entry.choice.warnings, protected: entry.choice.protected, images: entry.choice.images, long: entry.choice.long },
        counts: { postsPublished: entry.counts.postsPublished, postsRemoved: entry.counts.postsRemoved, imagesKept: entry.counts.imagesKept, imagesLeftOut: entry.counts.imagesLeftOut },
      })),
    ],
    // 2d (11.2): last, the account's Activity: the marker, the rules in the format's order, and every entry it received,
    // newest first and ungrouped, read page by page as it is written.
    [
      "activity",
      new Members([
        ["seenAt", plan.activity.seenAt],
        ["settings", { replies: plan.activity.settings.replies, mentions: plan.activity.settings.mentions, quotes: plan.activity.settings.quotes, follows: plan.activity.settings.follows }],
        ["received", new Paged(plan.activity.received, (entry: ReceivedEntry) => ({ kind: entry.kind, at: entry.at, postId: entry.postId, actorHandle: entry.actorHandle, shown: entry.shown }))],
      ]),
    ],
  ];

  yield* objectFragments(members, "");
}

/**
 * An object's members at the depth `pad` gives, as JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) writes them there: a list read in pages
 * element by element, an object of Members member by member, anything else stringified whole and indented to its depth.
 */
async function* objectFragments(members: [string, unknown][], pad: string): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  yield "{\n";
  for (const [index, [key, value]] of members.entries()) {
    yield `${index === 0 ? "" : ",\n"}${pad}  ${JSON.stringify(key)}: `;
    if (value instanceof Paged) yield* listFragments(value, `${pad}  `);
    else if (value instanceof Members) yield* objectFragments(value.members, `${pad}  `);
    else yield indented(JSON.stringify(value, null, 2), `${pad}  `);
  }
  yield `\n${pad}}`;
}

/** An object's members in the order of a format's shape, and no other member. */
function inShapeOrder<T extends object>(shape: object, value: T): T {
  const source = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(shape).map((key) => [key, source[key]])) as T;
}

/** The moderation member with every entry's members in the order of the format (ExportFormat in the contracts). */
function moderationMember(moderation: ModerationExport): ModerationExport {
  return {
    decisions: moderation.decisions.map((decision) => ({
      id: decision.id,
      decidedOn: decision.decidedOn,
      postId: decision.postId,
      kind: decision.kind,
      outcome: decision.outcome,
      ground: decision.ground,
      ruleId: decision.ruleId,
      rulesVersion: decision.rulesVersion,
      measures: decision.measures.map((measure) => ({ kind: measure.kind, mediaId: measure.mediaId, noEffect: measure.noEffect })),
      reversals: decision.reversals.map((reversal) => ({ kind: reversal.kind, mediaId: reversal.mediaId })),
      facts: decision.facts,
      reason: decision.reason,
      legalReference: decision.legalReference,
      appeal: decision.appeal === null ? null : decision.appeal.state === "pending" ? { state: "pending", result: null } : { state: "answered", result: decision.appeal.result },
      // 3f (W.7), and 3d review L14 (people12): an order's notice keeps its facts, the authority's words and the day of an
      // erasure, which the moderation module builds; absent on every other decision, as the format has them.
      ...(decision.order
        ? {
            order: inShapeOrder(OrderNoticeFacts.shape, decision.order),
            ...(decision.orderTexts ? { orderTexts: inShapeOrder(OrderTexts.shape, decision.orderTexts) } : {}),
            erasedOn: decision.erasedOn ?? null,
          }
        : {}),
      // 3d (W.10): what the statement says of automated means, and the objection to a program's measure with its time.
      automatedDetection: decision.automatedDetection,
      automatedDecision: decision.automatedDecision,
      signal: decision.signal === null ? null : { kind: decision.signal.kind, source: decision.signal.source, matchKind: decision.signal.matchKind, listedAs: decision.signal.listedAs, viewed: decision.signal.viewed },
      objection: decision.objection === null ? null : { text: decision.objection.text, createdAt: decision.objection.createdAt },
    })),
    reports: moderation.reports.map((report) => ({
      ref: report.ref,
      receivedAt: report.receivedAt,
      ground: report.ground,
      ruleId: report.ruleId,
      category: report.category,
      explanation: report.explanation,
      items: report.items.map((item) => ({ position: item.position, link: item.link, reexamines: item.reexamines, outcome: item.outcome, outcomeText: item.outcomeText, reexaminationOpen: item.reexaminationOpen })),
    })),
    // 3e (W.8): the strikes the account was given.
    strikes: moderation.strikes.map((strike) => ({ decisionId: strike.decisionId, postId: strike.postId, ruleId: strike.ruleId, givenAt: strike.givenAt, countsUntil: strike.countsUntil, overruledAt: strike.overruledAt })),
    // Then its suspensions, terminations and reporting measures, its replies to them, and its own reporting counts.
    standing: moderation.standing.map((entry) => ({
      decisionId: entry.decisionId,
      kind: entry.kind,
      basis: entry.basis,
      days: entry.days,
      announced: entry.announced,
      decidedAt: entry.decidedAt,
      earliestStart: entry.earliestStart,
      startsAt: entry.startsAt,
      endsAt: entry.endsAt,
      liftedAt: entry.liftedAt,
      liftedBy: entry.liftedBy,
      replaced: entry.replaced,
      basisEndedAt: entry.basisEndedAt,
      basisEndedBy: entry.basisEndedBy,
    })),
    replies: moderation.replies.map((reply) => ({ decisionId: reply.decisionId, filedAt: reply.filedAt, onTime: reply.onTime, text: reply.text, erasedAt: reply.erasedAt, answeredAt: reply.answeredAt, answeredBy: reply.answeredBy })),
    reporting: {
      frameDays: moderation.reporting.frameDays,
      days: moderation.reporting.days.map((entry) => ({ day: entry.day, reports: entry.reports })),
      marks: moderation.reporting.marks.map((mark) => ({ ref: mark.ref, position: mark.position, sentOn: mark.sentOn, markedAt: mark.markedAt, withdrawnAt: mark.withdrawnAt, counts: mark.counts })),
      markedReports: moderation.reporting.markedReports,
    },
    // 3d (W.10): the refused uploads as their notices read them, and the releases the account may be told of.
    uploads: moderation.uploads.map((upload) => ({
      id: upload.id,
      refusedAt: upload.refusedAt,
      source: upload.source,
      matchKind: upload.matchKind,
      listedAs: upload.listedAs,
      objection: upload.objection === null ? null : { text: upload.objection.text, objectedAt: upload.objection.objectedAt },
      mayObject: upload.mayObject,
      endedAt: upload.endedAt,
      endAs: upload.endAs,
      endReason: upload.endReason,
      released: upload.released,
      reportKept: upload.reportKept,
    })),
    releases: moderation.releases.map((release) => ({ id: release.id, basis: release.basis, releasedAt: release.releasedAt, upload: release.upload })),
  };
}

/** A member's array at the depth `pad` gives, as JSON.stringify writes it there: "[]" when empty, else one element per line group. */
async function* listFragments<T>(list: Paged<T>, pad: string): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  let first = true;
  for await (const page of list.pages) {
    for (const row of page) {
      yield `${first ? "[\n" : ",\n"}${pad}  ${indented(JSON.stringify(list.element(row), null, 2), `${pad}  `)}`;
      first = false;
    }
  }
  yield first ? "[]" : `\n${pad}]`;
}

const indented = (json: string, pad: string): string => json.replaceAll("\n", `\n${pad}`);

/**
 * Writes the archive: every image as a stored entry, then export.json, then the central directory.
 * export.json comes last so that missingMedia can name every image whose file the checked open refused
 * or did not find when its turn came (the sweeper may be between the row and the file), or that was no
 * longer the owner's to export by then: the media module reads each image's row again as it opens the
 * file, and opens none for an image deleted with its post, erased or sealed since the list was read.
 * The order of entries means nothing to a reader.
 */
export async function writeExport(writer: ZipWriter, plan: ExportPlan): Promise<void> {
  for (const image of plan.images) {
    if (!(await writer.addFile(mediaEntry(image.id), image.open))) plan.missingMedia.push(image.id);
  }
  await writer.addJsonPieces("export.json", exportJson(plan));
  await writer.end();
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The only file outside `src/account/` may import. Everything else in the module is private and the
 * architecture test fails the build if another file reaches into it.
 */
import type { MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { ActivityForAccount } from "../activity";
import type { AuthForAccount } from "../auth";
import type { ImportsForAccount } from "../imports";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import type { JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { MediaForAccount } from "../media";
import type { ModerationForAccount } from "../moderation";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { SocialForAccount } from "../social";
import type { AccountDeps } from "./context";
import { createPurgeJob } from "./purge";
import { accountRoutes } from "./routes";

export { AccountError } from "./context";
export type { AccountDeps } from "./context";

export interface CreateAccountOptions {
  /** The other modules' interfaces for this one, as their index files hand them out: auth.forAccount, social.forAccount, media.forAccount. */
  auth: AuthForAccount;
  social: SocialForAccount;
  media: MediaForAccount;
  /** The moderation module's interface for this one: moderation.forAccount. Without it the purge forgets no report's sender, and the export's moderation member is empty. */
  moderation?: ModerationForAccount;
  /** 3b Task 6: the imports module's interface for this one, imports.forAccount: the purge's step and the export's member. */
  imports?: ImportsForAccount;
  /** 2d: the activity module's interface for this one, activity.forAccount: the export's member `activity`. */
  activity?: ActivityForAccount;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's requireFreshAuth: a credential proven in the last five minutes, which the export needs. */
  requireFreshAuth: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's requireStrongFreshAuth: level 2 on an account with TOTP, which starting and confirming a deletion need (1c design, section 10). */
  requireStrongFreshAuth: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The daily export limit shares the store the per-IP middleware uses. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;
}

export function createAccount(options: CreateAccountOptions) {
  const deps: AccountDeps = {
    auth: options.auth,
    social: options.social,
    media: options.media,
    moderation: options.moderation,
    imports: options.imports,
    activity: options.activity,
    limits: options.rateLimitStore,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    routes: accountRoutes(deps, options.requireSession, options.requireFreshAuth, options.requireStrongFreshAuth),
    /** Starts the purge job (deletions left half done, every five minutes under the shared lock) and returns the function that stops it. */
    startPurge: (lock: JobLock) => createPurgeJob(deps, lock).start(),
  };
}

export type Account = ReturnType<typeof createAccount>;
```

```ts
import type { MeResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Hono } from "hono";
import { bodyLimit } from "hono/body-limit";
import { cors } from "hono/cors";
import { HTTPException } from "hono/http-exception";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { AccountError, type Account } from "./account";
import { ActivityError, type Activity } from "./activity";
import { AuthError, type Auth } from "./auth";
import type { Config } from "./config";
import type { AppEnv } from "./env";
import { ImportError, type Imports } from "./imports";
import { errorBody } from "./lib/errors";
import { MediaError, type Media } from "./media";
import { observability } from "./middleware/observability";
import { clientIpKey, rateLimit, type RateLimitStore } from "./middleware/rate-limit";
import { noStore, securityHeaders } from "./middleware/security-headers";
import { ModerationError, type Moderation } from "./moderation";
import { healthRoutes, type HealthChecks } from "./routes/health";
import { SocialError, type Social } from "./social";
import type { Staff } from "./staff";
import type { Transparency } from "./transparency";

/** JSON requests are small; the two raw upload routes count their own bytes and are exempt. */
export const JSON_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES = 64 * 1024;

/**
 * 3b (design, section 7.3): a chunk of an import's archive, PUT /api/imports/<id>/archive with the id as a lowercase
 * UUID's 36 characters, the pattern Caddy's @import_chunk matches. Its route counts the bytes against the chunk's own
 * rules, so it is the one route besides POST /api/media that the JSON body limit leaves alone.
 */
const IMPORT_CHUNK_PATH = /^[/]api[/]imports[/][0-9a-f-]{36}[/]archive$/;
const isRawUpload = (method: string, path: string): boolean => (method === "POST" && path === "/api/media") || (method === "PUT" && IMPORT_CHUNK_PATH.test(path));

/**
 * The staff console's paths (3a design, section 5): /api/staff and everything under it, never a path that merely begins
 * with the same letters. The app's CORS and session resolution pass over them, so a staff route never meets the app's
 * credentialed CORS, its Origin allow-list, its session or its CSRF check: the staff gate and the staff session are the
 * only origin and session logic there. Everything else in the chain (request id, access log, client identity, security
 * headers, no-store, the body limit, the global rate limit) applies to them as to any path.
 */
const isStaffPath = (path: string) => path === "/api/staff" || path.startsWith("/api/staff/");

export interface AppDeps {
  config: Config;
  logger: Logger;
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  healthChecks: HealthChecks;
  auth: Auth;
  /** Posting and feed. Optional so auth-only tests need no database for it; the server always wires it. */
  social?: Social;
  /** Image uploads. Optional for the same reason; the server always wires it. */
  media?: Media;
  /** The account lifecycle (the data export). Optional for the same reason; the server always wires it. */
  account?: Account;
  /** The staff console's API. Mounted only while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is set; optional as the other modules are. */
  staff?: Staff;
  /** Reports and notices. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it, whether the console is on or off. */
  moderation?: Moderation;
  /** Checks that report a part being down without marking the API unhealthy, the image worker for one. */
  advisoryChecks?: HealthChecks;
  /** 3d: the public figures' two routes. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it. */
  transparency?: Transparency;
  /** 3b: import from other platforms. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it. */
  imports?: Imports;
  /** 2d: Activity. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it. */
  activity?: Activity;
}

export function createApp({ config, logger, rateLimitStore, healthChecks, auth, social, media, account, staff, moderation, advisoryChecks, transparency, imports, activity }: AppDeps) {
  const app = new Hono<AppEnv>();

  app.use(observability(logger));
  app.use(auth.clientIdentity);
  app.use(securityHeaders, noStore);
  const appCors = cors({ origin: config.TRUSTED_ORIGINS, credentials: true });
  app.use((c, next) => (isStaffPath(c.req.path) ? next() : appCors(c, next)));
  const jsonBodies = bodyLimit({
    maxSize: JSON_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES,
    onError: (c) => c.json(errorBody("payload_too_large", "The request body is too large", (c as typeof c & { get(key: "requestId"): string }).get("requestId")), 413),
  });
  app.use((c, next) => (isRawUpload(c.req.method, c.req.path) ? next() : jsonBodies(c, next)));
  // Image files come before the global limit and session resolution: they have their own bucket,
  // and a public image needs no session. Everything else under /api/media falls through to below.
  if (media) app.route("/api/media", media.fileRoutes);
  app.use(rateLimit({ name: "global", store: rateLimitStore, limit: 300, windowMs: 60_000, key: clientIpKey }));
  // 3f (design, section 7.12): the status of a post's page, which Caddy asks for every view of /post/*, with the visitor's
  // cookies: after the global limit, which counts it against the visitor, and before the session's resolution, so it
  // reads no session. Every other path falls through to below.
  if (social) app.route("/api", social.statusRoutes);
  // 3d (design, sections 9.1 and 10.6): GET /api/public/facts and /api/public/transparency, at the same place and for the
  // same reasons: counted against the visitor by the global limit, and answered before any session is read. Each sets its
  // own Cache-Control, which noStore leaves alone.
  if (transparency) app.route("/api", transparency.routes);
  app.use((c, next) => (isStaffPath(c.req.path) ? next() : auth.resolveSession(c, next)));

  app.route("/api/health", healthRoutes(healthChecks, config.KORBAT_VERSION, advisoryChecks));
  app.route("/api/auth", auth.routes);
  // 3e (design, section 7.12): /api/me from the auth module's meFor and the moderation module's standingFor, read at
  // every request; null without the moderation module (an app built for some tests) or without a profile.
  app.get("/api/me", auth.requireOnboarding, async (c) => {
    const session = c.get("session")!;
    const base = await auth.meFor(session);
    const standing = moderation && base.profile !== null ? await moderation.standingFor(session.userId) : null;
    return c.json({ ...base, standing } satisfies MeResponse);
  });
  if (media) app.route("/api/media", media.routes);
  // 3b (design, section 9.1): every route behind the auth module's requireSession, CSRF included, like the social routes.
  if (imports) app.route("/api/imports", imports.routes);
  // 2d (design, section 9.2): every route behind the auth module's requireSession, CSRF included for the two writes.
  if (activity) app.route("/api/activity", activity.routes);

  if (staff && config.CONSOLE_ORIGIN !== undefined) app.route("/api/staff", staff.routes(config.CONSOLE_ORIGIN));
  // Reports and notices are taken, kept and given receipts whether or not the console is on: anyone may send one, signed
  // in or not, so these routes stand after session resolution and behind no session guard of their own.
  if (moderation) app.route("/api", moderation.routes);
  if (social) app.route("/api", social.routes);

  app.notFound((c) => c.json(errorBody("not_found", "No such route", c.get("requestId")), 404));
  app.onError((err, c) => {
    if (err instanceof AuthError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId"), err.details), err.status);

    if (err instanceof MediaError) return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    // 3b (design, sections 9.1 and 9.4): every refusal of an import with its status, never 500; wrong_offset carries the
    // stored size, so the app goes on from there.
    if (err instanceof ImportError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId"), err.details), err.status);
    }
    if (err instanceof SocialError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    }
    // 2d: a cursor of Activity that names no place; the limits of its two writes are the social module's (above).
    if (err instanceof ActivityError) return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    // The account routes render nothing themselves: their own errors and those of the three modules they call all land here.
    if (err instanceof AccountError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    }
    // A moderation flow's refusal, from the app's routes or from the console's case routes.
    if (err instanceof ModerationError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId"), err.details), err.status);
    }
    c.get("log").error({ err }, "unhandled error");
    return c.json(errorBody("internal", "Internal error", c.get("requestId")), 500);
  });

  return app;
}
```
