import { ModerationError, isModerationErrorCode, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { RETRY_MARGIN_MS } from "./decide";
import { appendConfirmedAudit, iso, raisedMessage, rows, staffCaseConflict, type Runner } from "./repo";

/**
 * The release (3d design, sections 6.2, 7.2, 7.14 and 9.6): the one-way end of korbat's keeping of the images of a seal
 * for good, on a leave or an instruction to destroy that the command line recorded, by an admin's confirmed action. The
 * database decides whether it can stand (seal_release, and releases_confirmed at commit); this file reads the release
 * block a case shows, runs the confirmed action's transaction, tells every staff account, and sends the author's notice
 * at once or, while a hold on telling stands, in the dispatch round that finds the last hold ended. It names no image
 * row: the release erases them inside the database's function, and the media module's disposal drops them.
 */

/** A time as ISO text in UTC, to the microsecond, for a list's cursor. */
const microsOf = (expression: string) => sql.raw(`to_char(${expression} at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')`);

interface FactsRow {
  reported: boolean;
  their_reference: string | null;
  answer: SealRelease["answer"];
  answered_at: string | null;
  handed_over_at: string | null;
  quarantined: boolean;
  preserved: boolean;
  leave_id: string | null;
  leave_from: "authority" | "court" | null;
  leave_reference: string | null;
  leave_received_on: string | null;
  leave_untold: boolean | null;
  leave_untold_until: string | null;
  tell_held: boolean;
}

/** The columns of release_facts and upload_release_facts that are an admin's alone. */
export interface AdminFactsRow {
  their_reference: string | null;
  answer: SealRelease["answer"];
  answered_at: string | null;
  leave_id: string | null;
  leave_from: "authority" | "court" | null;
  leave_reference: string | null;
  leave_received_on: string | null;
  leave_untold: boolean | null;
  leave_untold_until: string | null;
}

/**
 * 3d review M1 (design 11.4): the members of a release block that only an admin is given, the authority's reference, its
 * assessment with its day and the standing leave; for any other session none of them, not even as null, so a moderator
 * never learns them. The other facts (reported, in the quarantine, preserved, whether the notice would be held) stand.
 */
export function adminFacts(admin: boolean, f: AdminFactsRow): Pick<SealRelease, "theirReference" | "answer" | "answeredAt" | "leave"> {
  if (!admin) return {};
  return {
    theirReference: f.their_reference,
    answer: f.answer,
    answeredAt: f.answered_at,
    leave:
      f.leave_id === null
        ? null
        : { id: f.leave_id, from: f.leave_from!, reference: f.leave_reference!, receivedOn: f.leave_received_on!, untold: f.leave_untold === true, untoldUntil: f.leave_untold_until },
  };
}

/**
 * CaseDecision.release (sections 7.2, 8.5 and 10.3) for each of these seals for good in force, keyed by the seal's
 * ledger row: the facts of release_facts, the lowest RELEASE_POSTS_MAX posts of the seal not yet released (which the
 * params the key signs must name), how many more remain, silence_days, and the seal's newest release with its posts and
 * their image rows as the seal counted them.
 */
export async function releaseBlocks(q: Runner, actionIds: readonly string[], admin: boolean): Promise<Map<string, SealRelease>> {
  const blocks = new Map<string, SealRelease>();
  if (actionIds.length === 0) return blocks;
  const [rules] = await rows<{ silence_days: number | null }>(q, sql`select r.silence_days from public.release_rules() r`);
  for (const actionId of actionIds) {
    const [f] = await rows<FactsRow>(
      q,
      sql`select f.reported, f.their_reference, f.answer, ${iso("f.answered_at")} as answered_at, ${iso("f.handed_over_at")} as handed_over_at,
                 f.quarantined, f.preserved, f.leave_id, f.leave_from, f.leave_reference, to_char(f.leave_received_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as leave_received_on,
                 f.leave_untold, ${iso("f.leave_untold_until")} as leave_untold_until, f.tell_held
            from public.release_facts(${actionId}::uuid) f`,
    );
    const open = await rows<{ post_id: string }>(
      q,
      sql`select s.post_id from public.seal_posts s
           where s.action_id = ${actionId}::uuid and not exists (select 1 from public.release_posts r where r.post_id = s.post_id)
           order by s.post_id`,
    );
    const [newest] = await rows<{ released_at: string; basis: "leave" | "period"; backups_clear_at: string; held: boolean }>(
      q,
      sql`select ${iso("r.released_at")} as released_at, r.basis, ${iso("r.backups_clear_at")} as backups_clear_at, r.author_notice = 'held' as held
            from public.releases r where r.seal_action_id = ${actionId}::uuid order by r.released_at desc, r.id desc limit 1`,
    );
    const [released] = await rows<{ posts: number; images: number }>(
      q,
      sql`select count(*)::int as posts, coalesce(sum(s.images), 0)::int as images
            from public.seal_posts s join public.release_posts r on r.post_id = s.post_id where s.action_id = ${actionId}::uuid`,
    );
    const postIds = open.slice(0, RELEASE_POSTS_MAX).map((row) => row.post_id);
    blocks.set(actionId, {
      reported: f!.reported,
      ...adminFacts(admin, f!),
      handedOverAt: f!.handed_over_at,
      quarantined: f!.quarantined,
      preserved: f!.preserved,
      tellHeld: f!.tell_held,
      postIds,
      remaining: open.length - postIds.length,
      silenceDays: rules!.silence_days,
      releasedAt: newest?.released_at ?? null,
      basis: newest?.basis ?? null,
      backupsClearAt: newest?.backups_clear_at ?? null,
      noticeHeld: newest === undefined ? null : newest.held,
      releasedPosts: released!.posts,
      releasedImages: released!.images,
    });
  }
  return blocks;
}

/** The locks a release may wait for: the subject's profile, the case, the leave, the admin's auth row, the image rows and the audit head. */
const RELEASE_WAITS = 6;

/** What a release that committed answers: the seal's case, which the route answers as it now stands. */
export type ReleaseOutcome = { caseId: string; releaseId: string } | "ended" | "late";

/**
 * POST /api/staff/seals/:action/release, once its step-up verified (section 7.2): one transaction on the API's pool,
 * built as recordConfirmed builds a decision's. Every lock wait is bounded by what is left of the challenge; the subject's
 * profile FOR NO KEY UPDATE first, as in every deciding transaction; then seal_release, which takes the seal's case and
 * checks everything in the database's order; last the confirmed audit row seal_released on the seal, with the params as
 * the key confirmed them and the release's id, which releases_confirmed holds the row to at commit. "ended" and "late"
 * as for a decision; once more after a deadlock while the challenge has time. After the commit, unwaited for: the alert
 * seal_released to every staff account and the author's notice, unless it was born held.
 */
export async function releaseSeal(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<ReleaseOutcome> {
  // A confirmation of anything else never releases: a wiring fault, not a refusal.
  if (confirmed.action !== "seal_released" || confirmed.target.type !== "seal" || confirmed.keyId !== session.keyId) throw new Error("a seal is released only with the step-up that confirmed it");
  const params = SealReleasedParams.parse(confirmed.params);
  const actionId = confirmed.target.id;
  // A ledger row never changes: its subject and its case are read before the transaction, as decide reads a post's author.
  const [seal] = await rows<{ subject: string; case_id: string }>(
    deps.apiDb,
    sql`select a.subject_account_id as subject, d.case_id from public.decision_actions a join public.decisions d on d.id = a.decision_id
         where a.id = ${actionId}::uuid and a.kind::text = 'seal_media'`,
  );
  if (seal === undefined) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  // 3d review M2: an admin too close to the seal's subject is refused before anything is written, as every route that
  // names a case refuses (refuseRecused); seal_release refuses it again inside, whatever the API asks first.
  if (await staffCaseConflict(deps.apiDb, session.userId, seal.case_id)) throw new ModerationError("staff_recused");
  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      const message: StaffMessage = { template: "seal_released", facts: { at: deps.now().toISOString(), posts: params.postIds.length, uploads: 0 } };
      const outcome = await deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx): Promise<{ releaseId: string; rowId: number } | "late"> => {
        if (!(await boundLockWaits(tx, confirmed.expiresAt, RELEASE_WAITS))) return "late";
        await deps.social.lockAccounts(tx, [seal.subject], "no key update");
        const [row] = await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select public.seal_release(${actionId}::uuid, ${params.basis}, ${params.leaveId}::uuid, ${session.userId}::uuid) as id`);
        // 3d review L1: the alert's row in the release's own transaction, before its audit row: a restart after the commit
        // never loses it.
        const rowId = await confirmedAlertRow(tx, message);
        await appendConfirmedAudit(tx, {
          actorId: session.userId,
          keyId: confirmed.keyId,
          action: "seal_released",
          targetType: "seal",
          targetId: actionId,
          metadata: { params: confirmed.params, releaseId: row!.id },
          staffSession: session.handle,
          actionHash: confirmed.actionHash,
          stepUp: confirmed.assertion,
          requestId: ctx.requestId,
          expiresAt: confirmed.expiresAt,
        });
        return { releaseId: row!.id, rowId };
      });
      if (outcome === "late") return "late";
      deps.background.start(() => afterRelease(deps, outcome.releaseId, outcome.rowId, message));
      return { caseId: seal.case_id, releaseId: outcome.releaseId };
    } catch (err) {
      const refusal = raisedMessage(err);
      if (refusal === "staff_confirmation_ended") return "ended";
      if (refusal === "staff_confirmation_late") return "late";
      if (refusal !== null && isModerationErrorCode(refusal)) throw new ModerationError(refusal);
      if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isBoundReached(err)) throw err;
      if (attempt > 1 || confirmed.expiresAt.getTime() - deps.now().getTime() <= RETRY_MARGIN_MS) return "late";
    }
  }
}

/**
 * What follows a release's commit, each part in a try of its own (section 7.2, after the commit): the mail of the alert
 * seal_released to every staff account, the admin who released included, without a throttle (3c gives the milder lifting
 * of a seal the same), from the row the release's transaction wrote (3d review L1); then the author's notice, when it was
 * not born held. Never throws.
 */
async function afterRelease(deps: ModerationDeps, releaseId: string, rowId: number, message: StaffMessage): Promise<void> {
  await mailAlertRow(deps, rowId, message);
  try {
    await sendReleaseNotice(deps, releaseId);
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, releaseId }, "moderation: a release's notice was not sent; the dispatch round sends it");
  }
}

/** A mail's result as the notice's state. A relay that cannot take the mail now throws, and the notice stays pending. */
const NOTICE_STATE: Record<AccountMailResult, "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "failed"> = {
  sent: "sent",
  suppressed: "suppressed",
  no_address: "no_address",
  refused: "failed",
};

/** The release's author: the seal's subject, or for a replay the author of its posts; null when neither is there. */
const AUTHOR = (alias: string) =>
  sql.raw(`coalesce((select a.subject_account_id from public.decision_actions a where a.id = ${alias}.seal_action_id),
                    (select p.author_id from public.posts p where p.id = any(${alias}.post_ids) order by p.id limit 1))`);

/**
 * The view of a release that releaseNoticeParagraphs reads (ReleaseNoticeView), read for anyone or for its author alone
 * with `owner`; null for a release that is not there, not the owner's, or (unless `held` is allowed) whose notice is held.
 * `images` is the image rows the release erased, as the seals counted them (seal_posts.images, which nothing changes).
 */
export async function releaseView(
  q: Runner,
  releaseId: string,
  options: { owner?: string; allowHeld?: boolean; media?: Pick<ModerationDeps["media"], "refusalSubject"> } = {},
): Promise<(ReleaseNoticeView & { authorId: string | null }) | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ id: string; basis: "leave" | "period"; released_at: string; backups_clear_at: string; upload: boolean; upload_refusal_id: string | null; post_ids: string[]; author_id: string | null; held: boolean; seal_decision: string | null; images: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select r.id, r.basis, ${iso("r.released_at")} as released_at, ${iso("r.backups_clear_at")} as backups_clear_at, r.upload_refusal_id is not null as upload, r.upload_refusal_id,
               r.post_ids::text[] as post_ids, ${AUTHOR("r")} as author_id, r.author_notice = 'held' as held,
               coalesce((select a.decision_id from public.decision_actions a where a.id = r.seal_action_id),
                        (select a.decision_id from public.seal_posts s join public.decision_actions a on a.id = s.action_id
                          where s.post_id = any(r.post_ids) order by a.created_at desc, a.id limit 1)) as seal_decision,
               coalesce((select sum(x.images) from (select max(s.images) as images from public.seal_posts s where s.post_id = any(r.post_ids) group by s.post_id) x), 0)::int as images
          from public.releases r where r.id = ${releaseId}::uuid`,
  );
  if (row === undefined) return null;
  // 3d Task 7: a held upload's release has no seal and no post; its author is the refusal's uploader, read through the
  // media module, which owns the refusals.
  if (row.upload_refusal_id !== null) row.author_id = options.media === undefined ? null : ((await options.media.refusalSubject(q, row.upload_refusal_id))?.ownerId ?? null);
  if (options.owner !== undefined && row.author_id !== options.owner) return null;
  if (row.held && !options.allowHeld) return null;
  const posts = await rows<{ id: string; created_at: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select p.id, ${iso("p.created_at")} as created_at from public.posts p where p.id = any(${`{${row.post_ids.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]) order by p.created_at, p.id limit ${RELEASE_NOTICE_POSTS_MAX}`,
  );
  // 3d review L11 (people9): where the appeal of the sealing decision stands now, which the notice's paragraph on that
  // decision follows; one appeal a decision (appeals_once). A held upload's release has no such decision.
  const [appeal] =
    row.seal_decision === null || row.upload
      ? []
      : await rows<{ state: "pending" | "answered" }>(
          q,
          sql`select case when ap.answered_by is null then 'pending' else 'answered' end as state from public.appeals ap where ap.decision_id = ${row.seal_decision}::uuid`,
        );
  return {
    id: row.id,
    basis: row.basis,
    releasedAt: row.released_at,
    backupsClearAt: row.backups_clear_at,
    upload: row.upload,
    posts: posts.map((post) => ({ id: post.id, createdAt: post.created_at })),
    postCount: row.post_ids.length,
    images: row.images,
    sealDecisionId: row.seal_decision,
    appeal: appeal?.state ?? "none",
    authorId: row.author_id,
  };
}

/**
 * The author's notice of one release, if it is pending: in a transaction that holds the release's row FOR UPDATE while
 * the mail is sent, so the send after the commit and the dispatch round never both send it. The mail's result is the
 * notice's state; a relay that could not take it leaves it pending for the next round. Answers whether it was sent.
 */
export async function sendReleaseNotice(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth"> & { media?: ModerationDeps["media"] }, releaseId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
    const [locked] = await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select r.id from public.releases r where r.id = ${releaseId}::uuid and r.author_notice = 'pending' for update`);
    if (locked === undefined) return false;
    const view = await releaseView(tx, releaseId, { allowHeld: false, media: deps.media });
    if (view === null || view.authorId === null) {
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.releases set author_notice = 'none', author_notice_at = now() where id = ${releaseId}::uuid`);
      return false;
    }
    const { authorId, ...notice } = view;
    const state = NOTICE_STATE[await deps.auth.mailAccount(authorId, { template: "release_notice", view: notice })];
    await tx.execute(sql`update public.releases set author_notice = ${state}, author_notice_at = now() where id = ${releaseId}::uuid`);
    return state === "sent";
  });
}

/** How many releases' notices one round takes at most. */
const RELEASE_NOTICES_PER_ROUND = 50;
const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

/**
 * The dispatch round's releases (sections 7.2 and 7.14): first every held notice whose release the author may now be
 * told of (release_tellable) moves to pending, in the round that finds the last hold ended and never before, and is
 * mailed at once; then every pending notice the send after its commit left (older than `due`) is mailed, or given up
 * after the give-up days of 3c, counted from when it became pending. A row that fails is logged and left as it was.
 * Answers how many were sent.
 */
export async function releaseNotices(deps: ModerationDeps, now: Date, due: Date, logUnsent: (err: unknown, ids: Record<string, string>) => void): Promise<number> {
  let sent = 0;
  const held = await rows<{ id: string }>(deps.apiDb, sql`select r.id from public.releases r where r.author_notice = 'held' order by r.released_at, r.id limit ${RELEASE_NOTICES_PER_ROUND}`);
  for (const { id } of held) {
    try {
      const moved = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        deps.apiDb,
        sql`update public.releases set author_notice = 'pending', author_notice_at = now()
             where id = ${id}::uuid and author_notice = 'held' and public.release_tellable(id) returning id`,
      );
      if (moved.length > 0 && (await sendReleaseNotice(deps, id))) sent++;
    } catch (err) {
      logUnsent(err, { releaseId: id });
    }
  }
  const pending = await rows<{ id: string; since: string }>(
    deps.apiDb,
    sql`select r.id, ${iso("coalesce(r.author_notice_at, r.released_at)")} as since from public.releases r
         where r.author_notice = 'pending' and coalesce(r.author_notice_at, r.released_at) < ${due.toISOString()}::timestamptz
         order by r.released_at, r.id limit ${RELEASE_NOTICES_PER_ROUND}`,
  );
  for (const { id, since } of pending) {
    try {
      if (now.getTime() - Date.parse(since) > RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays * DAY_MS) {
        await deps.apiDb.execute(sql`update public.releases set author_notice = 'failed', author_notice_at = now() where id = ${id}::uuid and author_notice = 'pending'`);
        deps.log.warn({ kind: "release_notice", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
        continue;
      }
      if (await sendReleaseNotice(deps, id)) sent++;
    } catch (err) {
      logUnsent(err, { releaseId: id });
    }
  }
  return sent;
}

/**
 * The releases the author of `alias` may be told of: never one whose notice is held. The one rule of the Notices list
 * and (2d, 5.5.2) of Activity's entries, which read releases only through it.
 */
const toldRelease = (alias: string, viewer: string) => sql`${sql.raw(alias)}.author_notice <> 'held' and ${AUTHOR(alias)} = ${viewer}::uuid`;

/**
 * 2d (design, section 5.5.2): the releases about the viewer's posts as Activity lists them, by toldRelease as the Notices
 * list reads them, with the time that list shows (released_at) to the microsecond: newest first, by id among equal times,
 * released at or after `since`, after `after` (a time to the microsecond and an id) when given, at most `limit`.
 */
export async function activityReleases(q: Runner, viewer: string, after: { at: string; id: string } | null, since: string, limit: number): Promise<{ id: string; at: string }[]> {
  return rows<{ id: string; at: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select r.id, ${microsOf("r.released_at")} as at from public.releases r
         where ${toldRelease("r", viewer)} and r.released_at >= ${since}::timestamptz
           and (${after === null} or (r.released_at, r.id) < (${after?.at ?? null}::timestamptz, ${after?.id ?? null}::uuid))
         order by r.released_at desc, r.id desc limit ${limit}::int`,
  );
}

/**
 * GET /api/moderation/notices (sections 9.6 and 10.2): the releases about the viewer's posts, newest first, 20 a page,
 * never one whose notice is held: nothing of the app shows a release while a hold on telling stands.
 */
export async function authorNotices(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb"> & { media?: Pick<ModerationDeps["media"], "refusalsOf"> }, viewer: string, cursor?: string): Promise<AuthorNoticesPage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeListCursor(cursor);
  const releases = await rows<{ id: string; at: string; key: string }>(
    deps.apiDb,
    sql`select r.id, ${iso("r.released_at")} as at, ${microsOf("r.released_at")} as key
          from public.releases r
         where ${toldRelease("r", viewer)}
           and (${after === null} or (r.released_at, r.id) < (${after?.at ?? null}::timestamptz, ${after?.id ?? null}::uuid))
         order by r.released_at desc, r.id desc
         limit ${AUTHOR_NOTICES_PAGE_SIZE + 1}`,
  );
  // 3d Task 7 (sections 9.5 and 10.2): the viewer's refused uploads beside them, through the media module, merged newest
  // first under the one cursor of (time, id). A held upload's release is told in its own refusal's notice.
  const refusals = deps.media === undefined ? [] : await deps.media.refusalsOf(viewer, after, AUTHOR_NOTICES_PAGE_SIZE + 1);
  const found = [...releases.map((row) => ({ ...row, kind: "release" as const })), ...refusals.map((row) => ({ ...row, kind: "upload_refused" as const }))].sort((a, b) =>
    a.key !== b.key ? (a.key < b.key ? 1 : -1) : a.id < b.id ? 1 : a.id > b.id ? -1 : 0,
  );
  const page = found.slice(0, AUTHOR_NOTICES_PAGE_SIZE);
  const last = page[page.length - 1];
  return {
    notices: page.map((row) => ({ kind: row.kind, id: row.id, at: row.at })),
    nextCursor: found.length > AUTHOR_NOTICES_PAGE_SIZE && last ? encodeListCursor({ at: last.key, id: last.id }) : null,
  };
}

/**
 * 3d Task 8 (W.10): the export's `releases`: every release about the account's posts, and every release of one of its
 * refused uploads (given by id: the refusals are the media module's), newest first, each with its ground and its time and
 * whether it was of an upload. Never one whose notice is held: the export says no more than the notices may.
 */
export async function exportedReleases(q: Runner, viewer: string, refusalIds: readonly string[]): Promise<{ id: string; basis: "leave" | "period"; releasedAt: string; upload: boolean }[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string; basis: "leave" | "period"; released_at: string; upload: boolean }>(
    q,
    sql`select r.id, r.basis, ${iso("r.released_at")} as released_at, r.upload_refusal_id is not null as upload
          from public.releases r
         where r.author_notice <> 'held'
           and (${AUTHOR("r")} = ${viewer}::uuid or r.upload_refusal_id = any(${`{${refusalIds.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]))
         order by r.released_at desc, r.id desc`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, basis: row.basis, releasedAt: row.released_at, upload: row.upload }));
}

/** GET /api/moderation/releases/:release: the notice for its author alone, and not_found while it is held or for anyone else. */
export async function authorRelease(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, viewer: string, releaseId: string): Promise<ReleaseNoticeView> {
  const view = await releaseView(deps.apiDb, releaseId, { owner: viewer });
  if (view === null) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  const { authorId: _author, ...notice } = view;
  return notice;
}

/**
 * The appeals' mark (sections 7.2 and 8.7): for each of these decisions whose seal has released posts, the newest
 * release's time and ground, keyed by the decision's id.
 */
export async function releasedSeals(q: Runner, decisionIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, { at: string; basis: "leave" | "period" }>> {
  const marks = new Map<string, { at: string; basis: "leave" | "period" }>();
  if (decisionIds.length === 0) return marks;
  const found = await rows<{ decision_id: string; at: string; basis: "leave" | "period" }>(
    q,
    sql`select distinct on (a.decision_id) a.decision_id, ${iso("r.released_at")} as at, r.basis
          from public.decision_actions a join public.releases r on r.seal_action_id = a.id
         where a.decision_id = any(${`{${decisionIds.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]) and a.kind::text = 'seal_media'
         order by a.decision_id, r.released_at desc, r.id desc`,
  );
  for (const row of found) marks.set(row.decision_id, { at: row.at, basis: row.basis });
  return marks;
}

/** Home's [home.released] (sections 8.2 and 10.3): the releases of the last DESTRUCTIVE_DAYS, newest first, with their seal's case. */
export async function recentReleases(q: Runner, days: number, max: number): Promise<{ kind: "seal_released"; at: string; caseId: string | null; refusalId: null }[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ at: string; case_id: string | null }>(
    q,
    sql`select ${iso("r.released_at")} as at, d.case_id
          from public.releases r
          left join public.decision_actions a on a.id = r.seal_action_id
          left join public.decisions d on d.id = a.decision_id
         where r.replay_of is null and r.released_at >= now() - make_interval(days => ${days}::int)
         order by r.released_at desc, r.id desc limit ${max}`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => ({ kind: "seal_released" as const, at: row.at, caseId: row.case_id, refusalId: null }));
}

import { and, eq, isNotNull, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { handleHistory, profiles, type Db } from "@korbat/db";
import { handleRefusal, isUniqueViolation, type ProfileStore } from "../auth";
import { WRITE_CLOCK, liveNotSuspended } from "../lib/standing";

/**
 * Public profiles through the korbat_api pool. Onboarding writes the profile and the reservation of
 * its handle in one transaction; the unique index on lower(handle) and the primary key of
 * handle_history decide races and refuse a handle another profile holds or ever held. A handle korbat retired (3e) is
 * refused first, in the same transaction, with its own answer; the database's guard of handles refuses the same, and a
 * placeholder's form, under a race or to a caller that skipped the handle rule, and is answered alike.
 */
export function createProfileStore(apiDb: Db): ProfileStore {
  const columns = { id: profiles.id, handle: profiles.handle, displayName: profiles.displayName };
  return {
    async create({ id, handle, displayName }) {
      try {
        const profile = await apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
          // 3e: a retired handle is nobody's, so it is refused before the unique index would call it taken.
          const [retired] = await tx
            .select({ handle: handleHistory.handleLower })
            .from(handleHistory)
            .where(and(eq(handleHistory.handleLower, handle.toLowerCase()), isNotNull(handleHistory.retiredAt)))
            .limit(1);
          if (retired) return null;
          const [created] = await tx.insert(profiles).values({ id, handle, displayName }).returning(columns);
          // The handle chosen at onboarding is reserved like every later one (1b design, section 6); a row for it under another profile ends the transaction.
          await tx.insert(handleHistory).values({ handleLower: handle.toLowerCase(), profileId: id });
          return created!;
        });
        return profile === null ? { ok: false, reason: "handle_retired" } : { ok: true, profile };
      } catch (err) {
        const guarded = handleRefusal(err);
        if (guarded !== null) return { ok: false, reason: guarded };
        if (isUniqueViolation(err)) return { ok: false, reason: "handle_taken" };
        throw err;
      }
    },
    async find(id) {
      const [profile] = await apiDb
        .select({ ...columns, handleChangedAt: profiles.handleChangedAt, verifiedAt: profiles.verifiedAt, showInExplore: profiles.showInExplore, sharePreviews: profiles.sharePreviews })
        .from(profiles)
        .where(eq(profiles.id, id))
        .limit(1);
      if (!profile) return null;
      const { handleChangedAt, verifiedAt, showInExplore, sharePreviews, ...pub } = profile;
      // The badge is a fact of the profile row (verified_at), read here so the account screen sees it on /me; so is the
      // author's Explore switch, which the privacy screen shows and the public profile never carries, and (2d, decision
      // 21) the link-preview switch beside it.
      return { ...pub, handleChangedAt: handleChangedAt?.toISOString() ?? null, verified: verifiedAt !== null, showInExplore, sharePreviews };
    },
    /**
     * The badge, profiles.verified_at, which the auth module decides and cannot write. 3e (design, section 7.2): setting it
     * is a write of the account, so the one predicate joins the update's WHERE and the answer says whether a row changed;
     * removing it is open to everyone, and answers true. Setting it locks the row first, in a statement of its own, so the
     * UPDATE that judges comes once the row is held: an UPDATE that waited for a holder that only locked the row would
     * keep the judgment it made before the wait. It is the write's last statement, and so its closing judgment (3e's review).
     */
    async setVerified(id, at) {
      if (at === null) {
        await apiDb.update(profiles).set({ verifiedAt: null }).where(eq(profiles.id, id));
        return true;
      }
      return apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`select 1 from profiles where id = ${id}::uuid for no key update`);
        const updated = await tx.update(profiles).set({ verifiedAt: at }).where(and(eq(profiles.id, id), liveNotSuspended("profiles", WRITE_CLOCK))).returning({ id: profiles.id });
        return updated.length === 1;
      });
    },
    /** A plain read of the same fact, which startBadge asks first as a courtesy, so that no code is sent to a suspended account; the write decides. */
    async suspended(id) {
      const [row] = (await apiDb.execute(sql`select not ${liveNotSuspended("p", WRITE_CLOCK)} as suspended from profiles p where p.id = ${id}::uuid and p.deleted_at is null`)) as unknown as { suspended: boolean }[];
      return row?.suspended ?? false;
    },
  };
}

import type { EngagementResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { SocialError, type SocialDeps } from "../context";
import { enforceWriteLimit } from "../limits";
import { countsFor } from "../views";
import { ownProfile, targetPost } from "./posts";

export type EngagementKind = "like" | "repost" | "bookmark";

/**
 * Likes, reposts and bookmarks and their undos. Doing an action twice, or undoing one that was not
 * done, changes nothing and returns the current state. Only the action itself is rate limited, and
 * only the action consults the block relation: an undo removes the viewer's own row, whatever
 * stands between the accounts by then.
 */
export async function setEngagement(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string, postId: string, kind: EngagementKind, on: boolean): Promise<EngagementResponse> {
  if (on) {
    const target = await targetPost(deps, viewer, postId);
    const me = await ownProfile(deps, viewer);
    await enforceWriteLimit(deps.limits, viewer, kind, me.createdAt, deps.now());
    const other = target.authorId === viewer ? undefined : target.authorId;
    if (kind === "like") await deps.repo.like(viewer, postId, deps.now(), other);
    else if (kind === "repost") await deps.repo.repost(viewer, postId, deps.now(), other);
    else await deps.repo.bookmark(viewer, postId, deps.now());
  } else if (kind === "like") await deps.repo.unlike(viewer, postId);
  else if (kind === "repost") await deps.repo.unrepost(viewer, postId);
  else await deps.repo.unbookmark(viewer, postId);

  const row = (await deps.repo.findPosts([postId])).get(postId);
  if (!row) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  const state = (await deps.repo.viewerPostStates(viewer, [postId])).get(postId)!;
  // 2d (9.3): the answer's counts follow the views' one rule, so liking a post whose counts are hidden tells nothing.
  return { counts: countsFor(viewer, row), viewer: state };
}

import type { PostImage } from "../../media";
import { SocialError, type SocialDeps } from "../context";
import type { ExportKey, ExportPage, ExportedPostRow, HandleRefRow, PostRefRow } from "../repo";

/** An image on one of the exported posts, as the media module reports it; the account module names its file in the archive. */
export interface ExportedMedia {
  id: string;
  altText: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}

export type ExportedPost = ExportedPostRow & { media: ExportedMedia[] };

/**
 * The social module's part of the data export (1b design, section 7.5): the profile with every handle
 * it ever had and its Explore switch (2c design, section 8), every post it wrote whatever its state,
 * with its images (2d: and its mentions and hidden-counts switch), what it liked, reposted and
 * bookmarked, and the accounts it follows, blocks and mutes by the handle they have now. Times are
 * Dates here; the account module writes them as ISO text.
 *
 * The profile is read at once; each list is read page by page while the account module writes it, so
 * an account with many rows never has them all in memory. A list can be iterated more than once; each
 * iteration reads it again from the start.
 */
export interface ProfileExport {
  /** `retiredHandles` (3e design, W.8): the handles of the history that korbat retired and that are still retired, with when. */
  /** `sharePreviews` (2d design, section 11.2): the link-preview switch as it stands. */
  profile: { handle: string; displayName: string; bio: string; createdAt: Date; handleHistory: string[]; showInExplore: boolean; retiredHandles: { handle: string; retiredAt: Date }[]; sharePreviews: boolean };
  posts: AsyncIterable<ExportedPost[]>;
  likes: AsyncIterable<PostRefRow[]>;
  reposts: AsyncIterable<PostRefRow[]>;
  bookmarks: AsyncIterable<PostRefRow[]>;
  following: AsyncIterable<HandleRefRow[]>;
  blocks: AsyncIterable<HandleRefRow[]>;
  mutes: AsyncIterable<HandleRefRow[]>;
}

/** Rows per page of an export list: one statement each, and at most this many rows of a list in memory at once. */
export const EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE = 1_000;

/**
 * A list read in keyset pages, in (created_at, id) order: each page starts after the key of the last row
 * of the page before, and is read only once that page has been used. The walk ends at a page that is not
 * full.
 */
function paged<T>(read: (after: ExportKey | null) => Promise<ExportPage<T>>): AsyncIterable<T[]> {
  return {
    async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
      let after: ExportKey | null = null;
      do {
        const page: ExportPage<T> = await read(after);
        if (page.rows.length > 0) yield page.rows;
        after = page.next;
      } while (after !== null);
    },
  };
}

/**
 * Each page of posts with its images, fetched from the media module for that page's posts only. The author's own
 * withheld and removed images are listed like any other: they stay with their author. A sealed image is exported to
 * nobody, its author included, so the list does not name it (3c design, section 7.10), and the media module lists no
 * image of a deleted post and no erased image at all.
 */
function withMedia(deps: SocialDeps, pages: AsyncIterable<ExportedPostRow[]>): AsyncIterable<ExportedPost[]> {
  return {
    async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
      for await (const rows of pages) {
        const media: Map<string, PostImage[]> = await deps.media.forPosts(rows.map((post) => post.id));
        yield rows.map((post) => ({
          ...post,
          media: (media.get(post.id) ?? []).flatMap((image) => (image.state === "sealed" ? [] : [{ id: image.id, altText: image.alt, width: image.width, height: image.height }])),
        }));
      }
    },
  };
}

export async function exportProfile(deps: SocialDeps, userId: string, pageSize: number = EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE): Promise<ProfileExport> {
  const head = await deps.repo.exportHead(userId);
  if (!head) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);

  // handle_history holds the handle chosen at onboarding and every one later left behind, so the current handle
  // is there only when the account went back to one it had before; the list names every handle, the current one included.
  const handleHistory = [...head.handleHistory];
  const current = head.profile.handle.toLowerCase();
  if (!handleHistory.includes(current)) handleHistory.push(current);

  return {
    profile: {
      handle: head.profile.handle,
      displayName: head.profile.displayName,
      bio: head.profile.bio,
      createdAt: head.profile.createdAt,
      handleHistory,
      showInExplore: head.showInExplore,
      retiredHandles: head.retiredHandles,
      sharePreviews: head.sharePreviews,
    },
    posts: withMedia(
      deps,
      paged((after) => deps.repo.exportPosts(userId, after, pageSize)),
    ),
    likes: paged((after) => deps.repo.exportPostRefs(userId, "likes", after, pageSize)),
    reposts: paged((after) => deps.repo.exportPostRefs(userId, "reposts", after, pageSize)),
    bookmarks: paged((after) => deps.repo.exportPostRefs(userId, "bookmarks", after, pageSize)),
    following: paged((after) => deps.repo.exportHandleRefs(userId, "follows", after, pageSize)),
    blocks: paged((after) => deps.repo.exportHandleRefs(userId, "blocks", after, pageSize)),
    mutes: paged((after) => deps.repo.exportHandleRefs(userId, "mutes", after, pageSize)),
  };
}

import { mentionHandles, type CountsResponse, type CreatePostRequest, type Pagination, type PostView, type ThreadResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { isDeadlock } from "../../lib/lock-bounds";
import { SocialError, type SocialDeps, type ViewerId } from "../context";
import { decodeCursor } from "../cursor";
import { enforceWriteLimit } from "../limits";
import type { PostRow, ProfileRow } from "../repo";
import { isTombstone, loadPostViews, pageCursor, postView, postViews } from "../views";
import { postAccess } from "../visibility";

/** The viewer's own profile row; the tiers need its creation time. */
export async function ownProfile(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string): Promise<ProfileRow> {
  const profile = (await deps.repo.findProfiles([viewer])).get(viewer);
  if (!profile) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  return profile;
}

/**
 * A post the viewer wants to act on. The post's own state is judged first, so someone probing ids
 * learns nothing about hidden or deleted posts from a block. Then the refusal is directional: when
 * the viewer blocked the author it is `blocked`; when the author blocked the viewer it is
 * `hiddenCode`, which reveals nothing.
 */
export async function targetPost(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string, id: string, hiddenCode: "not_found" | "post_unavailable" = "not_found"): Promise<PostRow> {
  const hidden = () => new SocialError(hiddenCode, hiddenCode === "not_found" ? 404 : 400);
  const row = (await deps.repo.findPosts([id])).get(id);
  if (!row) throw hidden();
  if (postAccess(viewer, row, false) !== "shown") throw hidden();
  if (row.authorId !== viewer) {
    const relation = await deps.repo.relation(viewer, row.authorId);
    if (relation.blocked) throw new SocialError("blocked", 403);
    if (relation.blockedBy) throw hidden();
  }
  return row;
}

/**
 * A post, a reply or a quote by the viewer. 3e (design, section 5, the lock order, item 3): the repository takes the
 * author's row before the replied-to or quoted author's, and a purge takes its own row before its followers'; a quote of
 * the purged account's post by one of its followers can cross that purge, and PostgreSQL ends one of the two. The post's
 * transaction then changed nothing, so it is run once more: the second try finds the purge committed and answers as for
 * any deleted account. A second deadlock is the caller's.
 */
export async function createPost(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string, input: Omit<CreatePostRequest, "hideCounts"> & { hideCounts?: boolean }): Promise<PostView> {
  const me = await ownProfile(deps, viewer);
  const action = input.replyToId ? "reply" : input.quoteOfId ? "quote" : "post";
  const targetId = input.replyToId ?? input.quoteOfId;
  const target = targetId ? await targetPost(deps, viewer, targetId, "post_unavailable") : null;
  await enforceWriteLimit(deps.limits, viewer, action, me.createdAt, deps.now());
  // 2d (4.2): the handles the post names, read from the normalised body (CreatePostRequest normalised it) before the
  // transaction, which resolves them; the request's hidden-counts switch rides along.
  const mentions = mentionHandles(input.body);
  const write = () =>
    deps.repo.createPost({
      authorId: viewer,
      body: input.body,
      replyToId: input.replyToId ?? null,
      quoteOfId: input.quoteOfId ?? null,
      now: deps.now(),
      lockWith: target && target.authorId !== viewer ? target.authorId : null,
      mentions,
      // The route's request has it, off unless sent; a caller that builds the input itself may leave it out.
      hideCounts: input.hideCounts ?? false,
      within: (tx, postId) => deps.media.attach(tx, { postId, ownerId: viewer, items: input.media }),
    });
  const id = await onceMoreOnDeadlock(write);
  // 3d Task 6 (design, sections 5 and 7.9): after the commit, never inside its transaction, a post with images is handed
  // to the moderation module's automated step, which starts its task unwaited for and returns at once; a failure to start
  // it is logged, and the sweep finds the images' scores within a minute. The post's answer never waits for it.
  if (input.media.length > 0) {
    try {
      deps.moderation?.imagesPublished(id);
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, postId: id }, "posts: the automated step of a new post's images was not started; the sweep takes them");
    }
  }
  return (await postView(deps, viewer, id))!;
}

/** Runs a write, and once more when the database chose it to give way in a deadlock: it changed nothing (3e design, section 5). */
export async function onceMoreOnDeadlock<T>(write: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  try {
    return await write();
  } catch (err) {
    if (!isDeadlock(err)) throw err;
    return write();
  }
}

export async function getPost(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: ViewerId, id: string): Promise<PostView> {
  const view = await postView(deps, viewer, id);
  if (!view) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  return view;
}

/** Author only. Deleting twice is a no-op. Someone who may not see the post learns nothing. */
export async function deletePost(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string, id: string): Promise<void> {
  const row = (await deps.repo.findPosts([id])).get(id);
  // 3f (design, section 7.10): a post disabled for an authority's order answers its author as a post that does not
  // exist, so its deletion is not_found, as for anyone (the repository's update and posts_guard refuse it too).
  if (!row || row.state === "disabled") throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  if (row.authorId === viewer) {
    // The image rows go with the post, in its transaction. Their files are deleted after the commit: files cannot be rolled back.
    // The media module answers only the rows that are gone: an image a case holds as evidence, and every image of a frozen
    // post, keeps its row, served to nobody, and no deletion is asked for its files.
    let images: string[] = [];
    const remove = () =>
      deps.repo.deletePost(id, viewer, deps.now(), async (tx) => {
        images = await deps.media.detachAll(tx, id);
      });
    try {
      await remove();
    } catch (err) {
      // The deletion takes its posts in the order a report takes them, so the two never deadlock. An account's purge
      // still writes the counters of other accounts' posts in no order (its own comment says so), and the database may
      // end this transaction to break such a cycle. It has then changed nothing, so it is run once more: the author who
      // takes content down is not answered with an error for a wait that is over. A second deadlock is the caller's.
      if (!isDeadlock(err)) throw err;
      images = [];
      await remove();
    }
    await deps.media.requestDeletion(images);
    return;
  }
  const blocked = (await deps.repo.blockedEitherWay(viewer, [row.authorId])).has(row.authorId);
  if (postAccess(viewer, row, blocked) !== "shown") throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  throw new SocialError("not_author", 403);
}

/**
 * 2d (decision 26, 9.2): PATCH /api/posts/:id/counts, the author's switch of a post's like and repost counts. Counted
 * under hide-counts before anything is written. A post that is not the viewer's, is deleted or is disabled answers
 * not_found, as deletePost answers it; a withheld or removed one changes. Hiding is open to a suspended author, showing
 * again is refused account_suspended by the repository (lockActing).
 */
export async function setCountsHidden(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string, id: string, hidden: boolean): Promise<CountsResponse> {
  const me = await ownProfile(deps, viewer);
  await enforceWriteLimit(deps.limits, viewer, "hide-counts", me.createdAt, deps.now());
  if (!(await deps.repo.setHideCounts(id, viewer, hidden))) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  return { countsHidden: hidden };
}

/** The post, its ancestors root first (tombstones where needed), and a page of direct replies oldest first. */
export async function thread(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: ViewerId, id: string, query: Pagination): Promise<ThreadResponse> {
  const post = await getPost(deps, viewer, id);
  const ancestorIds = await deps.repo.ancestorIds(id);
  const loaded = await loadPostViews(deps, viewer, ancestorIds);
  const ancestors = ancestorIds.map((ancestorId) => loaded.get(ancestorId)!);
  const cursor = query.cursor ? decodeCursor(query.cursor) : undefined;
  const rows = await deps.repo.replies(id, viewer, cursor, query.limit);
  const items = await postViews(deps, viewer, rows);
  return { ancestors: ancestors.map((a) => (isTombstone(a) ? a : a)), post, replies: { items, nextCursor: pageCursor(rows, query.limit) } };
}

import type { HandleChangeRequest, ProfileEditRequest, ProfileView, SharePreviewsResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { checkHandle } from "../../auth";
import { SocialError, type SocialDeps } from "../context";
import { enforceAccountLimit, enforceWriteLimit } from "../limits";
import type { ProfileRow } from "../repo";
import { DAY_MS, HOUR_MS } from "../tiers";
import { profileView } from "./profiles";

/** A handle may change again this long after the last change (1b design, section 7.2). */
export const HANDLE_COOLDOWN_MS = 30 * DAY_MS;
/** Edits of the display name or the bio an account may make in an hour. */
export const PROFILE_EDITS_PER_HOUR = 10;

/** The viewer's own profile row, which the edits below start from. A session always has one; a missing row means the account is gone. */
async function own(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string): Promise<ProfileRow> {
  const row = await deps.repo.findProfileById(viewer);
  if (!row) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  return row;
}

/**
 * 2d (decision 21, 9.2): POST and DELETE /api/me/share-previews, the link-preview switch, as /me/explore answers its own.
 * Counted under share-previews first. Turning previews on is refused account_suspended while a suspension runs (the
 * repository's lockActing); turning them off only reduces what others see and is open to everyone.
 */
export async function setSharePreviews(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string, on: boolean): Promise<SharePreviewsResponse> {
  const row = await own(deps, viewer);
  await enforceWriteLimit(deps.limits, viewer, "share-previews", row.createdAt, deps.now());
  if (!(await deps.repo.setSharePreviews(viewer, on))) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  return { sharePreviews: on };
}

/** Sets the display name, the bio, or both, and answers with the profile as its owner sees it on the profile route. */
export async function editProfile(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string, input: ProfileEditRequest): Promise<ProfileView> {
  // The contract refuses an empty edit; a caller that skipped it gets the same answer instead of an update with nothing to set.
  if (input.displayName === undefined && input.bio === undefined) throw new SocialError("invalid_request", 400, "Nothing to change.");
  await enforceAccountLimit(deps.limits, "profile-edit", viewer, PROFILE_EDITS_PER_HOUR, HOUR_MS);
  if (!(await deps.repo.updateProfile(viewer, input))) {
    // 3e (design, section 7.2): the update itself decided, with the predicate in its WHERE. A live profile that it did
    // not change is one whose suspension runs; the refusal is whole, a patch that only blanks the bio included.
    const row = await deps.repo.findProfileById(viewer);
    throw row ? new SocialError("account_suspended", 403) : new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  }
  // The event says that the profile changed, not what it says now: the events table holds no content.
  await deps.events?.append(viewer, "profile_updated");
  const row = await own(deps, viewer);
  return profileView(row, await deps.repo.hasImported(row.id));
}

/**
 * Moves the account to a new handle: the handle rules and the reserved list first, then the 30-day
 * cooldown, then the repository's transaction, which decides whether the handle is free. The handle
 * left behind stays reserved for this account, which may take it back after the next cooldown.
 *
 * 3e (design, section 7.10): a handle korbat retired is refused to everyone, its former holder included
 * (handle_retired, 409), and the placeholder's prefix is in the reserved list. A retirement clears the
 * change time when it swaps the handle, so the first change after it meets no cooldown.
 */
export async function changeHandle(deps: SocialDeps, viewer: string, input: HandleChangeRequest): Promise<ProfileView> {
  const to = input.handle.toLowerCase();
  const problem = checkHandle(to);
  if (problem) throw new SocialError(problem, 400);
  const current = await own(deps, viewer);
  if (current.handle.toLowerCase() === to) throw new SocialError("invalid_request", 400, "That is already your handle.");
  const now = deps.now();
  if (current.handleChangedAt) {
    const allowedAt = current.handleChangedAt.getTime() + HANDLE_COOLDOWN_MS;
    // Retry-After says when the next change is allowed, in whole seconds and never zero.
    if (now.getTime() < allowedAt) throw new SocialError("handle_cooldown", 429, undefined, Math.max(1, Math.ceil((allowedAt - now.getTime()) / 1000)));
  }
  const result = await deps.repo.changeHandle(viewer, to, now);
  if (!result.ok) {
    if (result.reason === "handle_taken" || result.reason === "handle_retired") throw new SocialError(result.reason, 409);
    // The database's guard refused a placeholder's form that the handle rule let through: answered as that rule answers it.
    if (result.reason === "handle_reserved") throw new SocialError("handle_reserved", 400);
    // 3e: the locking statement found the account's suspension running; nothing was written.
    if (result.reason === "account_suspended") throw new SocialError("account_suspended", 403);
    // The row changed under us (a second request of the same account) and already holds this handle.
    if (result.reason === "unchanged") throw new SocialError("invalid_request", 400, "That is already your handle.");
    throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  }
  await deps.events?.append(viewer, "handle_changed", { from: result.from, to });
  const row = await own(deps, viewer);
  return profileView(row, await deps.repo.hasImported(row.id));
}

export interface SocialForModeration {

  postViews(viewer: string, postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostView>>;

 * built between the two.

export function socialForModeration(apiDb: Db): SocialForModeration {
  const repo = createSocialRepo(apiDb);
  return {
    lockAccounts: (tx, ids, mode, live) => repo.lockAccounts(tx, ids, mode, live),
    capturePost: (tx, postId) => repo.capturePost(tx, postId),
    captureProfile: (tx, accountId) => repo.captureProfile(tx, accountId),
    findAccountByHandle: (handle, withDeleted) => repo.findAccountByHandle(handle, withDeleted),

    postRef: (postId) => repo.postRef(postId),
  };

export interface CreateSocialOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** Per-account write limits share the store the per-IP middleware uses. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  logger: Logger;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's requireFreshAuth: a credential proven in the last five minutes, which a handle change needs on top. */
  requireFreshAuth: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's appendEvent, so profile and handle changes land in auth_events. Without it nothing is recorded (the 2a tests). */
  events?: SocialEvents;
  /** The media module's interface for posts. Without it posts carry no images. */
  media?: MediaForPosts;
  /** The moderation module's interface for views: moderation.forSocial. Without it no post carries the author's chip. */
  moderation?: ModerationForSocial;
  now?: () => Date;
}

export function createSocial(options: CreateSocialOptions) {
  const deps: SocialDeps = {
    repo: createSocialRepo(options.apiDb),
    media: options.media ?? WITHOUT_MEDIA,
    moderation: options.moderation,
    limits: options.rateLimitStore,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
    events: options.events,
  };
  const forAccount: SocialForAccount = {
    purgeProfile: (userId, now, within) => deps.repo.purgeProfile(userId, now, within),
    exportProfile: (userId, pageSize) => exportProfile(deps, userId, pageSize),
  };
  const forActivity: SocialForActivity = {
    async postViews(viewer, postIds) {
      const loaded = await loadPostViews(deps, viewer, [...postIds]);
      return new Map([...loaded].flatMap(([id, view]) => (isTombstone(view) ? [] : [[id, view] as const])));
    },
    async authors(ids) {
      const found = await deps.repo.findProfiles([...ids]);
      return new Map([...found].map(([id, profile]) => [id, authorOf(profile)] as const));
    },
  };
  const forImports: SocialForImports = {
    importedKeys: (ownerId, keys) => deps.repo.importedKeys(ownerId, keys),
    publishImportedBatch: (job, batch, now) => publishImportedBatch(deps, job, batch, now),
    removeImportedBatch: (job, now, limit) => removeImportedBatch(deps, job, now, limit),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    /** The interface the account module uses. */
    forAccount,
    /** 3b: the interface the imports module uses. */
    forImports,
    /** 2d: the interface the activity module uses. */
    forActivity,
    routes: socialRoutes(deps, options.requireSession, options.requireFreshAuth),
    /**
     * 3f (design, section 7.12): GET /api/posts/:id/status, a router of its own that app.ts mounts after the global limit
     * and before the session's resolution. No interface member: nothing outside this module calls it.
     */
    statusRoutes: postStatusRoutes(deps),
    /**
     * Starts the Explore refresh under the shared job lock: a round at once, then one every five minutes. Returns the
     * function that stops the timer.
     */
    startExplore: (lock: JobLock) => startExplore(deps, lock),
  };
}

export type Social = ReturnType<typeof createSocial>;

/**

 * Two rules keep the counters and the pagination exact:
 * - every counter changes in the same transaction as the action, by the number of rows the action
 *   really inserted or deleted, so repeating an action never double-counts;
 * - every timestamp is passed in from the clock (millisecond precision) instead of the database
 *   default, so a keyset cursor built from a row round-trips exactly.
 *
 * Reads take the viewer (or null when signed out) and apply the visibility rule in SQL: others see
 * only visible posts, the author also sees their own withheld and removed posts, a block in either
 * direction hides an author entirely, and mutes apply to timelines only.
 *
 * Reads are raw SQL through `db.execute`, which returns timestamps as text and expands a JavaScript
 * array into a parameter list. So timestamps are formatted as ISO text in SQL and parsed once in
 * the row mappers, and id lists travel as one comma-joined parameter split back into a uuid array.
 */

export interface AuthorRow {
  id: string;
  handle: string;
  displayName: string;
  verified: boolean;
}

export interface PostRow {
  id: string;
  authorId: string;
  body: string;

  replyToAuthorId: string | null;

   * (never its second); null for a native post and for a tombstone, whose columns are cleared.

  imported: { source: ImportSource; at: string; shortened: boolean } | null;
  /** 2d (decision 26): the author hid the like and repost counts from everyone else. */
  hideCounts: boolean;
}

/** One line of a list: which post, when it sorts, and who reposted it (timelines only). */
export interface ListRow {
  postId: string;
  sortAt: Date;
  reposterId: string | null;
}

export interface ProfileRow {
  id: string;
  handle: string;
  displayName: string;

  followingCount: number;
  postCount: number;

  /** When the handle last changed after onboarding, null until then; the next change waits 30 days. */
  handleChangedAt: Date | null;
}

/** How a handle change ended: the handle the profile had before, or why nothing was written. */
export type HandleChangeResult = { ok: true; from: string } | { ok: false; reason: "not_found" | "unchanged" | "handle_taken" | "handle_retired" | "handle_reserved" | "account_suspended" };

/** A post as its author wrote it, for the data export; a deleted one keeps its row with an empty body and its deletion time. */
export interface ExportedPostRow {
  id: string;
  body: string;
  createdAt: Date;
  replyToId: string | null;
  quoteOfId: string | null;
  state: StoredPostState;
  deletedAt: Date | null;
  /** 3b (design, section 11.2): an imported post's source, the date its archive gave it and whether it was shortened. */
  imported: { source: ImportSource; originalCreatedAt: Date; shortened: boolean } | null;
  /** 2d (design, section 11.2): the handles its stored mentions name as written, in text order, and its hidden-counts switch. */
  mentions: string[];
  countsHidden: boolean;
}

/**
 * 3b (design, section 6.5): the import a batch belongs to, as the imports module read it. The batch is written only while
 * the job is still publishing at `cursor`, the post_cursor the caller read.
 */
export interface ImportBatchJob {
  id: string;
  ownerId: string;
  source: ImportSource;
  cursor: number;
}

/** One post of an import's batch, built by the imports module from a line the person's choice keeps (imports/plan.ts). */
export interface ImportBatchPost {
  /** importPostId(seed, ref): derived, so a parent's id is computed and a repeated batch inserts nothing twice. */
  id: string;
  /** importPostId(seed, parent) for a line of the account's own thread, else null; written top-level when that post is not there. */
  parentId: string | null;
  body: string;

  originalCreatedAt: string;

  key: string;

  images: { id: string; alt: string }[];
}

/** A batch's outcome: nothing written (the import moved on, or another batch wrote it), or the posts it inserted. */
export type ImportBatchResult = { written: false } | { written: true; posts: { id: string; images: boolean }[] };

/** An undo batch's outcome: the posts it found to remove, those it tombstoned, and the image rows that went with them. */
export interface RemoveBatchResult {
  selected: number;
  removed: number;
  images: string[];
}

/** Something the account did to a post (a like, a repost, a bookmark), and when. */
export interface PostRefRow {
  postId: string;
  at: Date;
}

/** The other side of a graph relation by the handle it has now (nothing else about them), and since when. */
export interface HandleRefRow {
  handle: string;
  since: Date;
}

/**
 * Where a page of the data export ends: the last row's created_at to the microsecond, as ISO text, and its
 * id (the post's, or the other account's). The next page starts after it. The microseconds matter: a row
 * written by a database default carries them, and a key cut to the millisecond would read such rows twice
 * or skip them.
 */
export interface ExportKey {
  at: string;
  id: string;
}

/** One page of a list for the data export, and the key to read the next one after, or null when this page was the last. */
export interface ExportPage<T> {
  rows: T[];
  next: ExportKey | null;
}

export interface Relation {
  following: boolean;
  followedBy: boolean;
  /** The viewer blocks the other account. */
  blocked: boolean;
  /** The other account blocks the viewer. */
  blockedBy: boolean;
  muted: boolean;
}

export interface ViewerPostRow {
  liked: boolean;
  reposted: boolean;
  bookmarked: boolean;
}

export interface ProfileListRow {
  profileId: string;
  sortAt: Date;
}

/**
 * What a round of the Explore refresh did: nothing, because the newest ranking is younger than the formula's minimum
 * gap, or a new ranking under `generation` with the posts that passed the candidate predicate, the posts it holds and
 * the milliseconds it took.
 */
export type ExploreRefresh = { skipped: true } | { skipped: false; generation: number; candidates: number; items: number; tookMs: number };

/** One row of an Explore page: the post, and its place in the ranking, which orders the page and is never answered. */
export interface ExploreRow {
  postId: string;
  position: number;
}

/**
 * What one statement found for a page of Explore: the current generation (null before the first round); the ranking
 * read, the cursor's or else the current one, with its time, when it is kept (null otherwise); the position of the
 * cursor's post in that ranking (null when the ranking does not hold it; 0 without a cursor); and the rows after that
 * position that pass the page's filters, in order, at most the limit asked for.
 */
export interface ExplorePageRead {
  current: number | null;
  ranking: { generation: number; asOf: Date } | null;
  after: number | null;
  rows: ExploreRow[];
}

/**
 * What the author's status needs to know about one post before any judgement: who wrote it, whether it is a reply or a
 * quote, whether it is visible, whether its author is suspended now (3e), whether its author shows in Explore, whether
 * its window has passed at the request time, and the current ranking, if there is one, with its time, its formula's
 * version, whether it holds the post, whether the post was written after it and whether moderation gave the post back
 * after it (3e).
 */
export interface ExploreFacts {
  authorId: string;
  reply: boolean;
  quote: boolean;
  /** 3b (design, sections 8.5 and 10.6): an imported post, which enters no feed on its own. */
  imported: boolean;
  visible: boolean;
  suspended: boolean;
  shown: boolean;
  outsideWindow: boolean;
  ranking: { generation: number; asOf: Date; formula: number; holdsPost: boolean; postIsNewer: boolean; restoredSince: boolean } | null;
}

/**
 * The status's judgement of one post: whether it meets every rule of the formula as of the request time and as of the
 * ranking's time (null when the ranking was computed under another version of the formula, whose rules are not judged),
 * and how many places the ranking gives the post's author and holds in all.
 */
export interface ExploreJudgement {
  metNow: boolean;
  metAtRanking: boolean | null;
  authorPlaces: number;
  places: number;
}

/**
 * The modes a profile row is locked in for a moderation case: a decision's on its subject (3e: `update` when it takes or
 * may start a suspension or a termination, section 5's lock order; `no key update` otherwise), and a report's on its sender.
 */
export type AccountLockMode = "update" | "no key update" | "key share";

/** One row lockAccounts locked: whether its account is deleted, and, read in the same statement by the clock, suspended and restricted in its reports. */
export interface LockedAccount {
  id: string;
  deleted: boolean;
  suspended: boolean;
  reportsRestricted: boolean;
}

/** A post as a case's evidence copies it. `body` is empty when the post's content was erased (`erased`). */
export interface CapturedPost {
  id: string;
  authorId: string;
  authorHandle: string;
  body: string;
  state: StoredPostState;
  createdAt: Date;
  replyToId: string | null;
  quoteOfId: string | null;
  erased: boolean;
}

/** An account's profile fields as a case's evidence copies them. */
export interface CapturedProfile {
  id: string;
  handle: string;
  displayName: string;
  bio: string;
  deleted: boolean;
}

interface RawCapturedPost {
  id: string;
  author_id: string;
  author_handle: string;
  body: string;
  state: StoredPostState;
  created_at: string;
  reply_to_id: string | null;
  quote_of_id: string | null;
  erased: boolean;
}

export const MAX_ANCESTORS = 50;
const NO_REPOSTER = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000";

interface RawPost {
  id: string;
  author_id: string;
  body: string;
  reply_to_id: string | null;
  quote_of_id: string | null;
  state: StoredPostState;
  like_count: number;
  repost_count: number;
  reply_count: number;
  quote_count: number;
  created_at: string;
  deleted_at: string | null;
  author_handle: string;
  author_display_name: string;
  author_verified: boolean;
  reply_to_handle: string | null;
  reply_to_author_id: string | null;
  reply_to_state: StoredPostState | null;
  import_source: ImportSource | null;
  original_day: string | null;
  import_shortened: boolean | null;
  hide_counts: boolean;
}

interface RawListRow {
  post_id: string;
  sort_at: string;
  reposter_id: string | null;
}

interface RawProfileListRow {
  profile_id: string;
  sort_at: string;
}

interface RawProfile {
  id: string;
  handle: string;
  display_name: string;
  bio: string;
  verified: boolean;
  follower_count: number;
  following_count: number;
  post_count: number;
  created_at: string;
  handle_changed_at: string | null;
}

/** A row of the Explore page statement: the page's facts on every row, and a post on each row but a lone one for an empty page. */
interface RawExplorePage {
  current: number | null;
  generation: number | null;
  as_of: string | null;
  after: number | null;
  post_id: string | null;
  position: number | null;
}

interface RawExploreFacts {
  author_id: string;
  reply: boolean;
  quote: boolean;
  imported: boolean;
  visible: boolean;
  suspended: boolean;
  shown: boolean;
  outside_window: boolean;
  generation: number | null;
  as_of: string | null;
  formula: number | null;
  holds_post: boolean;
  newer: boolean | null;
  restored: boolean;
}

/** A timestamptz expression as ISO text with milliseconds, in UTC. The expression is a column reference written here, never input. */
const iso = (column: string): SQL => sql.raw(`to_char(${column} at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"')`);

/** The same with the microseconds a timestamp column holds, for the export's page keys, which must round-trip exactly. */
const isoMicro = (column: string): SQL => sql.raw(`to_char(${column} at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')`);

/** Rows after `after` in (created_at, id) order: the keyset condition of an export page. Always true for the first page. */
const exportAfter = (after: ExportKey | null, at: SQL, id: SQL): SQL => (after ? sql`(${at}, ${id}) > (${after.at}::timestamptz, ${after.id}::uuid)` : sql`true`);

/** The page a query answered, with its next key when the page is full (a full page may be followed by more). */
function exportPage<R extends { key_at: string; key_id: string }, T>(raw: R[], limit: number, map: (row: R) => T): ExportPage<T> {
  const last = raw.at(-1);
  return { rows: raw.map(map), next: raw.length === limit && last ? { at: last.key_at, id: last.key_id } : null };
}

/** A list of ids as one parameter, split into a uuid array in SQL. */
const uuidArray = (ids: string[]): SQL => sql`string_to_array(${ids.join(",")}, ',')::uuid[]`;

/** 3b (design, sections 6.2 and 6.5): the five import columns as a tombstone writes them, all null at once, as posts_import_guard allows only there. */
const CLEARED_IMPORT = { importJobId: null, importSource: null, originalCreatedAt: null, importShortened: null, importKey: null } as const;

const toPost = (r: RawPost): PostRow => ({
  id: r.id,
  authorId: r.author_id,
  body: r.body,
  replyToId: r.reply_to_id,
  quoteOfId: r.quote_of_id,
  state: r.state,
  likeCount: r.like_count,
  repostCount: r.repost_count,
  replyCount: r.reply_count,
  quoteCount: r.quote_count,
  createdAt: new Date(r.created_at),
  deletedAt: r.deleted_at ? new Date(r.deleted_at) : null,
  author: { id: r.author_id, handle: r.author_handle, displayName: r.author_display_name, verified: r.author_verified },
  replyToHandle: r.reply_to_handle,
  replyToAuthorId: r.reply_to_author_id,
  replyToState: r.reply_to_state,
  imported: r.import_source !== null && r.original_day !== null ? { source: r.import_source, at: r.original_day, shortened: r.import_shortened === true } : null,
  hideCounts: r.hide_counts,
});

const toListRow = (r: RawListRow): ListRow => ({ postId: r.post_id, sortAt: new Date(r.sort_at), reposterId: r.reposter_id });

const toProfileListRow = (r: RawProfileListRow): ProfileListRow => ({ profileId: r.profile_id, sortAt: new Date(r.sort_at) });

const toProfile = (r: RawProfile): ProfileRow => ({
  id: r.id,
  handle: r.handle,
  displayName: r.display_name,
  bio: r.bio,
  verified: r.verified,
  followerCount: r.follower_count,
  followingCount: r.following_count,
  postCount: r.post_count,
  createdAt: new Date(r.created_at),
  handleChangedAt: r.handle_changed_at ? new Date(r.handle_changed_at) : null,
});

/** `p` is the posts alias in every read below. */
const visibleTo = (viewer: string | null): SQL =>
  viewer === null
    ? sql`p.state = 'visible'`
    : sql`(p.state = 'visible' or (p.author_id = ${viewer}::uuid and p.state in ('withheld', 'removed')))`;

/** No block in either direction between the viewer and the author of `p`. */
const authorNotBlocked = (viewer: string | null): SQL =>
  viewer === null
    ? sql`true`
    : sql`not exists (select 1 from blocks b where (b.blocker_id = ${viewer}::uuid and b.blocked_id = p.author_id) or (b.blocked_id = ${viewer}::uuid and b.blocker_id = p.author_id))`;

/** No block in either direction with the author or the reposter of a timeline item `i`. */
const itemNotBlocked = (viewer: string | null): SQL =>
  viewer === null
    ? sql`true`
    : sql`not exists (select 1 from blocks b where (b.blocker_id = ${viewer}::uuid and b.blocked_id in (i.author_id, i.reposter_id)) or (b.blocked_id = ${viewer}::uuid and b.blocker_id in (i.author_id, i.reposter_id)))`;

const itemNotMuted = (viewer: string | null): SQL =>
  viewer === null ? sql`true` : sql`not exists (select 1 from mutes m where m.muter_id = ${viewer}::uuid and m.muted_id in (i.author_id, i.reposter_id))`;

/** Raw queries take timestamps as ISO text, never as Date objects. */
const at = (cursor: Cursor): string => new Date(cursor.t).toISOString();

const before = (cursor: Cursor | undefined, sortAt: SQL, id: SQL): SQL =>
  cursor ? sql`(${sortAt}, ${id}) < (${at(cursor)}::timestamptz, ${cursor.id}::uuid)` : sql`true`;

const after = (cursor: Cursor | undefined, sortAt: SQL, id: SQL): SQL =>
  cursor ? sql`(${sortAt}, ${id}) > (${at(cursor)}::timestamptz, ${cursor.id}::uuid)` : sql`true`;

const beforeItem = (cursor: Cursor | undefined): SQL =>
  cursor
    ? sql`(i.sort_at, i.post_id, coalesce(i.reposter_id, ${NO_REPOSTER}::uuid)) < (${at(cursor)}::timestamptz, ${cursor.id}::uuid, ${cursor.r ?? NO_REPOSTER}::uuid)`
    : sql`true`;

const POST_COLUMNS = sql`p.id, p.author_id, p.body, p.reply_to_id, p.quote_of_id, p.state, p.like_count, p.repost_count, p.reply_count, p.quote_count,
  ${iso("p.created_at")} as created_at, ${iso("p.deleted_at")} as deleted_at,
  a.handle as author_handle, a.display_name as author_display_name, (a.verified_at is not null) as author_verified,
  rp.handle as reply_to_handle, pp.author_id as reply_to_author_id, pp.state as reply_to_state,
  p.import_source::text as import_source, to_char(p.original_created_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') as original_day, p.import_shortened, p.hide_counts`;
const POST_JOINS = sql`from posts p join profiles a on a.id = p.author_id left join posts pp on pp.id = p.reply_to_id left join profiles rp on rp.id = pp.author_id`;
const PROFILE_COLUMNS = sql`id, handle, display_name, bio, (verified_at is not null) as verified, follower_count, following_count, post_count, ${iso("created_at")} as created_at, ${iso("handle_changed_at")} as handle_changed_at`;
const PROFILE_SELECT = sql`select ${PROFILE_COLUMNS} from profiles`;

/** No block in either direction between the viewer and the account `other` names (a column reference). */
const otherNotBlocked = (viewer: string | null, other: SQL): SQL =>
  viewer === null
    ? sql`true`
    : sql`not exists (select 1 from blocks b where (b.blocker_id = ${viewer}::uuid and b.blocked_id = ${other}) or (b.blocked_id = ${viewer}::uuid and b.blocker_id = ${other}))`;

/** The viewer neither blocks, is blocked by, nor mutes the account `other` names. */
const otherWelcome = (viewer: string, other: SQL): SQL =>
  sql`${otherNotBlocked(viewer, other)} and not exists (select 1 from mutes m where m.muter_id = ${viewer}::uuid and m.muted_id = ${other})`;

/** A keyset bound on the three sort columns of a timeline branch. */
const beforeTriple = (cursor: Cursor | undefined, sortAt: SQL, id: SQL, reposter: SQL): SQL =>
  cursor ? sql`(${sortAt}, ${id}, ${reposter}) < (${at(cursor)}::timestamptz, ${cursor.id}::uuid, ${cursor.r ?? NO_REPOSTER}::uuid)` : sql`true`;

/** The outer select of a list query whose inner query `i` carries post_id, sort_at and reposter_id. */
const LIST_COLUMNS = sql`i.post_id, ${iso("i.sort_at")} as sort_at, i.reposter_id`;

/** Durations built in SQL from the formula's numbers, so each number travels as a parameter. */
const hours = (n: number): SQL => sql`(${n}::float8 * interval '1 hour')`;
const minutes = (n: number): SQL => sql`(${n}::float8 * interval '1 minute')`;

/** The one version of the Explore formula whose rules exploreRules writes (3e design, section 7.13). */
const EXPLORE_RULES_VERSION = 2;

/**
 * The time Explore's reads (the page, the chip and the author's status) judge an author's suspension by (3e design,
 * section 7.13 item 6): the database's clock when the statement reads, the same clock a write is judged by. A round
 * judges by its own time instead (exploreRules).
 */
const READ_CLOCK = WRITE_CLOCK;

/**
 * The rules of one Explore formula as of one time (2c design, section 7; 3e design, section 7.13: version 2), as SQL
 * fragments. The refresh ranks with them and the author's status judges one post with them, so the two cannot disagree;
 * the time and every number of the formula travel as parameters. `post` narrows the candidates and the engagement to one
 * post, which the status reads through that post's own indexes; the rules are the same either way. A formula of any
 * other version throws here, before any SQL, so no ranking is stored under a version whose rules were not applied.
 *
 * Version 2's two rules: an account suspended at the time `asOf` (the round's own time, never the clock) is neither a
 * candidate's author nor an engager, by the one predicate of lib/standing.ts applied to rows the round only reads; and a
 * post's window and age count from coalesce(explore_from, created_at), its `starts_at`, where explore_from is created_at
 * plus every span moderation kept the post hidden, which the database's moderation_apply alone writes.
 */
function exploreRules(asOf: Date, formula: ExploreFormula) {
  if (formula.version !== EXPLORE_RULES_VERSION) {
    throw new Error(`Explore's round applies the rules of formula version ${EXPLORE_RULES_VERSION} only, not version ${formula.version}`);
  }
  const at = sql`${asOf.toISOString()}::timestamptz`;
  // A candidate is younger than the window, and only engagement inside the window counts.
  const since = sql`${at} - ${hours(formula.windowHours)}`;
  // Engagement counts once it has stood this long, so a like made just before a round and undone after it never counts.
  const settled = sql`${at} - ${minutes(formula.standingMinutes)}`;
  const onePost = (column: SQL, post?: string): SQL => (post ? sql` and ${column} = ${post}::uuid` : sql.empty());
  /**
   * The one candidate predicate: visible top-level posts that are not quotes, by authors who are live and not suspended
   * at the time and have not switched Explore off, whose starts_at lies in the window up to the time. The window test is
   * written in two arms so that each uses its own index: a post never given back its time by its created_at, a restored
   * one by its explore_from (a partial index holds only those). 3b (design, sections 1.5 and 8.5; decision 8): an imported
   * post is never a candidate; it enters no feed on its own, and is published all at once by design.
   */
  const candidates = (post?: string): SQL => sql`
    select p.id, p.author_id, coalesce(p.explore_from, p.created_at) as starts_at from posts p join profiles a on a.id = p.author_id
    where p.reply_to_id is null and p.quote_of_id is null and p.state = 'visible' and p.import_job_id is null
      and ((p.explore_from is null and p.created_at > ${since} and p.created_at <= ${at}) or (p.explore_from > ${since} and p.explore_from <= ${at}))
      and ${liveNotSuspended("a", at)} and a.show_in_explore${onePost(sql`p.id`, post)}`;
  /**
   * The engagement that counts, read from the candidates `c`: likes and reposts in the window that have stood long enough,
   * by accounts other than the author that are live and not suspended at the time and were old enough when they engaged.
   * The engager is judged at the round, never at the time of the like: a ring's earlier likes stop counting at once.
   */
  const engagement = (post?: string): SQL => sql`
    select x.post_id, x.user_id from (
      select post_id, user_id, created_at from likes where created_at > ${since} and created_at <= ${settled}${onePost(sql`post_id`, post)}
      union all
      select post_id, user_id, created_at from reposts where created_at > ${since} and created_at <= ${settled}${onePost(sql`post_id`, post)}
    ) x
    join c on c.id = x.post_id
    join profiles u on u.id = x.user_id
    where x.user_id <> c.author_id and ${liveNotSuspended("u", at)} and u.created_at <= x.created_at - ${hours(formula.engagerMinAgeHours)}`;
  /** The approving accounts per post, read from the engagement `e`: each counted once however it engaged, for the posts that reach the threshold. */
