```ts
        const images: string[] = [];
        for (const row of gone) images.push(...(await detach(tx, row.id)));
        await tx.execute(sql`update import_jobs set posts_removed = posts_removed + ${gone.length}::int where id = ${job.id}::uuid`);
        return { selected: batch.length, removed: gone.length, images };
      });
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ deletion

    /**
     * Everything the account owns or is part of in this module goes in one transaction (1b design,
     * section 7.6): its posts become tombstones as after a deletion by the author, with the reply
     * counters of their parents and the quote counters of what they quoted adjusted for those not
     * tombstoned already; its likes, reposts and bookmarks go with the counters of their posts; its
     * follows go in both directions with the other side's counters; its blocks and mutes go in both
     * directions; the profile row stays, anonymised, with its handle, so the handle is never reused.
     * `within` runs in the same transaction, as its last act, for the media rows. The profile row is locked first, so a
     * second purge of the same account (the request's and the job's) waits for the first and then finds
     * nothing left: every statement below changes only what is still there, so a repeat changes nothing.
     * The same lock orders the purge against every write by or about the account (a follow, like, repost,
     * bookmark, block, mute, post, reply or quote), which takes a shared lock on the row (lockLive): one that
     * comes second waits for the purge and is refused, one that comes first makes the purge wait and has what
     * it wrote removed or tombstoned here (a reply or a quote by another account stays, as one written before
     * the deletion would). After the profile row come the row locks of every post of the account, in id order,
     * before any post is written (3c design, section 7.10): a report that holds two of them holds them in that
     * order. What stays unordered are the counters of other accounts' posts that this account replied to, quoted,
     * liked or reposted, which are written after.
     *
     * 3e (design, section 5, the lock order, item 3): right after its own row, the purge takes the rows of every account
     * whose counter it will write (those it follows and its followers) FOR NO KEY UPDATE, in id order, before any post.
     * With the posts first, a decision holding its subject FOR UPDATE, a third account's reply and a follower's purge
     * formed a cycle. An unfollow, a second follow or a quote between the purged account and its own counterparts can
     * still cross it; PostgreSQL detects that, the flows of follow, unfollow and createPost try once more, and the purge
     * is tried again by its job's next round.
     */
    async purgeProfile(id: string, now: Date, within: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
      await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        const [row] = (await tx.execute(sql`select handle from profiles where id = ${id}::uuid for update`)) as unknown as { handle: string }[];
        await tx.execute(sql`
          select p.id from profiles p
           where p.id <> ${id}::uuid
             and p.id in (select followee_id from follows where follower_id = ${id}::uuid union select follower_id from follows where followee_id = ${id}::uuid)
           order by p.id for no key update`);
        // Every post of the account is locked first, in id order, before any of them is written. A report holds the posts it
        // copies for share in that order, and one about a post that quotes or replies to its author's own post holds two
        // posts of this account. The counter statements below write such a quoted or replied-to post, in their scan's
        // order, and the tombstones write the rest: with the locks taken here, in the report's order, the purge either
        // waits at the first post the report holds, holding none itself, or holds them all before the report asks. The
        // deleted posts are locked too: a live post may quote or reply to one, and its counter is written all the same.
        await tx.execute(sql`select id from posts where author_id = ${id}::uuid order by id for update`);
        // The counters come off first, from the posts about to go, in one statement each: a self-reply's parent is a post of the author's too, and a row may be written once per statement.
        await tx.execute(sql`
          update posts set reply_count = greatest(0, reply_count - c.n)
          from (select reply_to_id, count(*)::int as n from posts where author_id = ${id}::uuid and state <> 'deleted_by_author' and reply_to_id is not null group by reply_to_id) c
          where posts.id = c.reply_to_id`);
        await tx.execute(sql`
          update posts set quote_count = greatest(0, quote_count - c.n)
          from (select quote_of_id, count(*)::int as n from posts where author_id = ${id}::uuid and state <> 'deleted_by_author' and quote_of_id is not null group by quote_of_id) c
          where posts.id = c.quote_of_id`);
        // 3f (design, section 5, the lock order, item 4): the profile row is anonymised (which sets deleted_at) before the
        // tombstones, so posts_guard lets the tombstone of a post disabled for an order through, as it does only for a
        // deleted account. The row is this transaction's from its first statement, so no lock moves. The handle stays on
        // the row and is reserved in handle_history like one left behind, so nobody can take it whatever becomes of the
        // row; it may be there already, from an earlier stint. Only a live row is written, so a repeat leaves the deletion
        // time alone.
        if (row) await tx.insert(handleHistory).values({ handleLower: row.handle.toLowerCase(), profileId: id, changedAt: now }).onConflictDoNothing();
        await tx
          .update(profiles)
          .set({ displayName: "Deleted account", bio: "", avatarPath: null, verifiedAt: null, followerCount: 0, followingCount: 0, postCount: 0, deletedAt: now })
          .where(and(eq(profiles.id, id), isNull(profiles.deletedAt)));
        // The tombstones. The rows are this transaction's already, and no post of the account can appear meanwhile: writing
        // one takes a shared lock on the profile row, which this transaction holds for update. 3b (design, sections 4.7 and
        // 6.6): the five import columns are cleared in the same statement, a disabled post's too (the profile is marked
        // deleted above), and on any tombstone that still carries them, which keeps its deletion time; then no post names
        // an import of the account, whose rows the caller's `within` deletes.
        await tx.execute(sql`
          update posts set state = 'deleted_by_author', deleted_at = case when state = 'deleted_by_author' then deleted_at else ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz end, body = '',
                 import_job_id = null, import_source = null, original_created_at = null, import_shortened = null, import_key = null
           where author_id = ${id}::uuid and (state <> 'deleted_by_author' or import_job_id is not null)`);
        // The account's own engagement, with the counters of the posts it was on; bookmarks count nothing.
        await tx.execute(sql`
          with gone as (delete from likes where user_id = ${id}::uuid returning post_id)
          update posts set like_count = greatest(0, like_count - c.n) from (select post_id, count(*)::int as n from gone group by post_id) c where posts.id = c.post_id`);
        await tx.execute(sql`
          with gone as (delete from reposts where user_id = ${id}::uuid returning post_id)
          update posts set repost_count = greatest(0, repost_count - c.n) from (select post_id, count(*)::int as n from gone group by post_id) c where posts.id = c.post_id`);
        await tx.delete(bookmarks).where(eq(bookmarks.userId, id));
        // The graph, both ways, with the other side's counters; the account's own counters are zeroed with the row below.
        await tx.execute(sql`
          with gone as (delete from follows where follower_id = ${id}::uuid returning followee_id)
          update profiles set follower_count = greatest(0, follower_count - c.n) from (select followee_id, count(*)::int as n from gone group by followee_id) c where profiles.id = c.followee_id`);
        await tx.execute(sql`
          with gone as (delete from follows where followee_id = ${id}::uuid returning follower_id)
          update profiles set following_count = greatest(0, following_count - c.n) from (select follower_id, count(*)::int as n from gone group by follower_id) c where profiles.id = c.follower_id`);
        await tx.delete(blocks).where(or(eq(blocks.fromId, id), eq(blocks.toId, id)));
        await tx.delete(mutes).where(or(eq(mutes.fromId, id), eq(mutes.toId, id)));
        // 2d (4.4, 5.6, 6.7): after the tombstones, the mentions that name the account and those of its own posts, every
        // Activity entry it caused or received, and its seen marker and rules. A post in flight that mentions it took its
        // row FOR KEY SHARE (createPost's lookup), so it either committed first, and its rows go here, or waits and then
        // finds the account deleted and stores nothing.
        await tx.execute(sql`delete from post_mentions where account_id = ${id}::uuid or post_id in (select p.id from posts p where p.author_id = ${id}::uuid)`);
        await tx.execute(sql`delete from activity_items where recipient_id = ${id}::uuid or actor_id = ${id}::uuid`);
        await tx.execute(sql`delete from activity_state where account_id = ${id}::uuid`);
        // The media rows go last (3c design, section 7.10): they are the last rows this transaction locks, after every
        // post and profile row it takes, and the requests for their files, which cannot be rolled back, are written as
        // close to the commit as they can be.
        await within(tx);
      });
    },
  };
}

type Tx = Parameters<Parameters<Db["transaction"]>[0]>[0];

/**
 * Serializes the writes between two accounts for the rest of the transaction: follow, block, like,
 * repost, reply and quote all take it, so none of them can land while a block between the pair is
 * being written. The key is the unordered pair, hashed; a collision only means extra waiting.
 */
async function pairLock(tx: Tx, a: string, b: string): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`select pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(least(${a}, ${b})), hashtext(greatest(${a}, ${b})))`);
}

/** Takes the pair lock and refuses, with `code`, when a block exists between the two in either direction. */
async function guardPair(tx: Tx, me: string, other: string, code: "not_found" | "post_unavailable"): Promise<void> {
  if (me === other) return;
  await pairLock(tx, me, other);
  const found = await tx.execute(
    sql`select 1 from blocks where (blocker_id = ${me}::uuid and blocked_id = ${other}::uuid) or (blocker_id = ${other}::uuid and blocked_id = ${me}::uuid) limit 1`,
  );
  if (found.length > 0) throw new SocialError(code, code === "not_found" ? 404 : 400);
}

/**
 * Takes these posts' rows, in id order and in one statement, in the mode an update of a counter or of the state takes
 * them: what a transaction that writes more than one post does before it writes the first, so that every such
 * transaction and every report that copies the same posts (for share, in id order) meet at the lowest post they share,
 * where the one that comes second holds none of the others yet. An id no post has locks nothing.
 */
async function lockPostsInOrder(tx: Tx, ids: readonly (string | null)[]): Promise<void> {
  const wanted = [...new Set(ids.filter((id): id is string => id !== null))];
  if (wanted.length === 0) return;
  await tx.execute(sql`select id from posts where id = any(${uuidArray(wanted)}) order by id for no key update`);
}

/** The profile rows an engagement is about, for lockLive: the account acting and the author of the post (one row when they are the same). */
function actorAndAuthor(userId: string, postId: string): SQL {
  return sql`id = ${userId}::uuid or id = (select author_id from posts where id = ${postId}::uuid)`;
}

/**
 * Locks the profile rows `accounts` selects for the rest of the transaction and refuses the write, with the
 * guard's `code` (not_found unless said), when one of them is deleted. The account purge holds its row `for
 * update` for its whole transaction, so a write that comes second waits and then sees the deletion, and a
 * purge that comes second waits for the write and then removes what it wrote. The lock is `for key share`,
 * the weakest that conflicts with `for update`: `for share` would also conflict with the counter updates
 * these same transactions make on the row (an update takes `for no key update`), so two follows of one
 * account at once would each hold the lock the other's update waits for, and deadlock.
 *
 * 3e (design, section 7.2): `acting` is the account that writes (the engager of a like, a repost or a bookmark); the
 * locking statement answers for each row whether its suspension runs, and the write is refused account_suspended when the
 * acting account's does. Any other row need only be live. A block and a mute name no acting account: both stay open.
 */
async function lockLive(tx: Tx, accounts: SQL, code: "not_found" | "post_unavailable" = "not_found", acting: string | null = null): Promise<void> {
  const found = (await tx.execute(
    sql`select id, deleted_at is not null as deleted, ${suspendedAt("profiles", WRITE_CLOCK)} as suspended from profiles where ${accounts} for key share`,
  )) as unknown as { id: string; deleted: boolean; suspended: boolean }[];
  if (found.some((row) => row.deleted)) throw new SocialError(code, code === "not_found" ? 404 : 400);
  if (acting !== null && found.some((row) => row.id === acting && row.suspended)) throw new SocialError("account_suspended", 403);
}

/**
 * The author's own row for a new post, in its own statement and in the mode its counter needs (3e design, section 5, the
 * lock order, item 2), with the predicate on it: a deleted author is refused not_found, a suspended one account_suspended.
 */
async function lockActing(tx: Tx, accountId: string, mode: "no key update" | "key share"): Promise<void> {
  // The mode is one of two literals of this file, never input.
  const [row] = (await tx.execute(
    sql`select deleted_at is not null as deleted, ${suspendedAt("profiles", WRITE_CLOCK)} as suspended from profiles where id = ${accountId}::uuid for ${sql.raw(mode)}`,
  )) as unknown as { deleted: boolean; suspended: boolean }[];
  if (!row || row.deleted) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  if (row.suspended) throw new SocialError("account_suspended", 403);
}

/**
 * The closing judgment of a write of `accountId` (lib/standing.ts): the transaction's last statement. A deleted account is
 * refused not_found, a suspended one account_suspended, either of which rolls the write back.
 */
async function judgeActing(tx: Tx, accountId: string): Promise<void> {
  const judged = await closingJudgment(tx, accountId);
  if (!judged || judged.deleted) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  if (judged.suspended) throw new SocialError("account_suspended", 403);
}

/**
 * Both profile rows of a follow or an unfollow FOR NO KEY UPDATE, the mode their counter updates take, in one statement
 * ordered by id (3e design, section 5, the lock order, item 2). A deleted row is refused not_found when `acting` is given
 * (a follow), and the acting account's running suspension account_suspended; an unfollow refuses neither.
 */
async function lockPair(tx: Tx, a: string, b: string, acting: string | null): Promise<void> {
  const found = (await tx.execute(
    sql`select id, deleted_at is not null as deleted, ${suspendedAt("profiles", WRITE_CLOCK)} as suspended from profiles where id in (${a}::uuid, ${b}::uuid) order by id for no key update`,
  )) as unknown as { id: string; deleted: boolean; suspended: boolean }[];
  if (acting === null) return;
  if (found.some((row) => row.deleted)) throw new SocialError("not_found", 404);
  if (found.some((row) => row.id === acting && row.suspended)) throw new SocialError("account_suspended", 403);
}

/** Removes `userId`'s reposts and likes of `authorId`'s posts and takes them off the counters, in the same transaction. */
async function retractEngagement(tx: Tx, userId: string, authorId: string): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`
    with gone as (delete from reposts r using posts p where r.post_id = p.id and r.user_id = ${userId}::uuid and p.author_id = ${authorId}::uuid returning r.post_id)
    update posts set repost_count = greatest(0, repost_count - c.n) from (select post_id, count(*)::int as n from gone group by post_id) c where posts.id = c.post_id`);
  await tx.execute(sql`
    with gone as (delete from likes l using posts p where l.post_id = p.id and l.user_id = ${userId}::uuid and p.author_id = ${authorId}::uuid returning l.post_id)
    update posts set like_count = greatest(0, like_count - c.n) from (select post_id, count(*)::int as n from gone group by post_id) c where posts.id = c.post_id`);
}

async function removeFollow(tx: Tx, followerId: string, followeeId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const deleted = await tx.delete(follows).where(and(eq(follows.fromId, followerId), eq(follows.toId, followeeId))).returning({ toId: follows.toId });
  if (deleted.length > 0) {
    await tx.update(profiles).set({ followerCount: sql`greatest(0, ${profiles.followerCount} - 1)` }).where(eq(profiles.id, followeeId));
    await tx.update(profiles).set({ followingCount: sql`greatest(0, ${profiles.followingCount} - 1)` }).where(eq(profiles.id, followerId));
  }
  return deleted.length > 0;
}

/**
 * 2d (design, section 5.3): who a new post tells, as rows (recipient_id, kind) for writeEntries. The parent's author for
 * a reply, the quoted author for a quote, then the stored mentions by position with the author and the accounts already
 * listed removed, cut to MENTION_NOTIFY_MAX; one row per recipient, the first in that order (reply, then quote, then
 * mention), so a reply that also names its parent's author is one reply entry. Only the parent's author is told of a
 * reply, never the thread's root or its other authors. The cut comes before the recipients' rules, so whether the
 * eleventh mention is told never depends on the first ten's settings.
 */
function postCandidates(authorId: string, postId: string, replyToId: string | null, quoteOfId: string | null): SQL {
  return sql`
    with listed as (
      select p.author_id as recipient_id, 'reply'::text as kind, 0 as place from posts p where p.id = ${replyToId}::uuid
      union all
      select p.author_id, 'quote', 1 from posts p where p.id = ${quoteOfId}::uuid
    ),
    named as (
      select m.account_id as recipient_id, 'mention'::text as kind, 2 + m.position as place from post_mentions m
       where m.post_id = ${postId}::uuid and m.account_id <> ${authorId}::uuid and m.account_id not in (select l.recipient_id from listed l)
       order by m.position limit ${MENTION_NOTIFY_MAX}
    )
    select distinct on (t.recipient_id) t.recipient_id, t.kind from (select * from listed union all select * from named) t order by t.recipient_id, t.place`;
}

/**
 * 2d (design, sections 5.2 and 5.3): the one statement that writes Activity entries, for createPost's candidates and for
 * a follow's one. `candidates` answers rows (recipient_id, kind); each becomes an entry of `actorId`'s act (about
 * `postId`, or none for a follow) only when every rule of the recipient holds, read in the act's own transaction: the
 * recipient is not the actor and is not deleted; no block stands between them either way; the recipient does not mute
 * the actor (decision 8); and the recipient's setting for the kind lets the actor in (activity_state, the defaults
 * Everyone and On without a row): `everyone`; `older` when the actor's account was made at least ACTIVITY_MIN_AGE_HOURS
 * before the act, judged by now(), the transaction's start, which is also the time activity_items_insert gives the entry,
 * against profiles.created_at; `following` when the recipient follows the actor; for a follow, `follows`. A refused rule
 * writes nothing. The unique keys make a repeat write nothing (`on conflict do nothing`). The time is the database's.
 */
async function writeEntries(tx: Tx, actorId: string, postId: string | null, candidates: SQL): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`
    with c as (${candidates})
    insert into activity_items (recipient_id, kind, actor_id, post_id)
    select c.recipient_id, c.kind::activity_kind, ${actorId}::uuid, ${postId}::uuid
      from c
      join profiles r on r.id = c.recipient_id and r.deleted_at is null
      cross join (select a.created_at from profiles a where a.id = ${actorId}::uuid) actor
      left join activity_state s on s.account_id = c.recipient_id
     where c.recipient_id <> ${actorId}::uuid
       and not exists (select 1 from blocks b where (b.blocker_id = c.recipient_id and b.blocked_id = ${actorId}::uuid) or (b.blocker_id = ${actorId}::uuid and b.blocked_id = c.recipient_id))
       and not exists (select 1 from mutes m where m.muter_id = c.recipient_id and m.muted_id = ${actorId}::uuid)
       and case when c.kind = 'follow' then coalesce(s.follows, true)
                else case coalesce(case c.kind when 'reply' then s.replies::text when 'quote' then s.quotes::text else s.mentions::text end, 'everyone')
                       when 'everyone' then true
                       when 'older' then actor.created_at <= now() - make_interval(hours => ${ACTIVITY_MIN_AGE_HOURS}::int)
                       when 'following' then exists (select 1 from follows f where f.follower_id = c.recipient_id and f.followee_id = ${actorId}::uuid)
                       else false end end
    on conflict do nothing`);
}

export type SocialRepo = ReturnType<typeof createSocialRepo>;
```

```ts
import { CountsRequest, CreatePostRequest, HandleChangeRequest, HandleParam, Pagination, PostId, ProfileEditRequest } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Hono, type Context, type MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import { z } from "zod";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import { errorBody } from "../lib/errors";
import { validate } from "../lib/validate";
import { MediaError } from "../media";
import { SocialError, type SocialDeps, type ViewerId } from "./context";
import { setEngagement, type EngagementKind } from "./flows/engagement";
import { explorePage, exploreStatus, setShowInExplore } from "./flows/explore";
import { blockedList, mutedList, setBlock, setFollow, setMute } from "./flows/graph";
import { createPost, deletePost, getPost, setCountsHidden, thread } from "./flows/posts";
import { changeHandle, editProfile, setSharePreviews } from "./flows/profile-edit";
import { followers, following, profile } from "./flows/profiles";
import { bookmarkedPosts, followingTimeline, latestTimeline, likedPosts, profileImported, profilePosts, profileReplies } from "./flows/timelines";

const PostParam = z.object({ id: PostId });
const ProfileParam = z.object({ handle: HandleParam });

/** Signed out, Explore is its first page only (2c design, section 8): a cursor asks for more, which needs an account. */
const EXPLORE_SIGN_IN = "Sign in to see more of Explore.";

/**
 * Every social endpoint, mounted at `/api`. Handlers only validate, call a flow and shape the
 * response. `guard` is the auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account, with CSRF and
 * Origin already checked for cookie sessions. `fresh` is its requireFreshAuth: a credential proven
 * in the last five minutes, which a handle change needs on top.
 */
export function socialRoutes(deps: SocialDeps, guard: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>, fresh: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>) {
  const r = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  const viewer = (c: Context<AppEnv>): ViewerId => c.get("session")?.userId ?? null;
  const me = (c: Context<AppEnv>): string => c.get("session")!.userId;

  r.onError((err, c) => {
    if (err instanceof SocialError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    }
    // Creating a post attaches its images through the media module, which refuses with its own error type.
    if (err instanceof MediaError) return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    c.get("log").error({ err }, "unhandled error in social route");
    return c.json(errorBody("internal", "Internal error", c.get("requestId")), 500);
  });

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- posts

  r.post("/posts", guard, validate("json", CreatePostRequest), async (c) => c.json(await createPost(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("json")), 201));
  // 2d (decision 26, 9.2): the author's hidden-counts switch of a post, before the post's deletion in the route table.
  r.patch("/posts/:id/counts", guard, validate("param", PostParam), validate("json", CountsRequest), async (c) =>
    c.json(await setCountsHidden(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id, c.req.valid("json").hidden)),
  );
  r.get("/posts/:id", validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => c.json(await getPost(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").id)));
  r.delete("/posts/:id", guard, validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => {
    await deletePost(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id);
    return c.body(null, 204);
  });
  r.get("/posts/:id/thread", validate("param", PostParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await thread(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").id, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  // Why the author's own post is in Explore or not; anyone else gets not_found from the flow.
  r.get("/posts/:id/explore", guard, validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => c.json(await exploreStatus(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id)));

  for (const kind of ["like", "repost", "bookmark"] as EngagementKind[]) {
    r.post(`/posts/:id/${kind}`, guard, validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => c.json(await setEngagement(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id, kind, true)));
    r.delete(`/posts/:id/${kind}`, guard, validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => c.json(await setEngagement(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id, kind, false)));
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- timelines

  r.get("/timeline/following", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await followingTimeline(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/timeline/latest", validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await latestTimeline(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/timeline/explore", validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => {
    const query = c.req.valid("query");
    // Refused here, before the flow reads anything: whatever the cursor holds, a signed-out reader gets the first page only.
    if (!viewer(c) && query.cursor) return c.json(errorBody("unauthenticated", EXPLORE_SIGN_IN, c.get("requestId")), 401);
    return c.json(await explorePage(deps, viewer(c), query));
  });

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- profiles and graph

  r.get("/profiles/:handle", validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await profile(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").handle)));
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/posts", validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await profilePosts(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/replies", validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await profileReplies(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  // 3b (design, section 9.2): the Imported tab, public as the Posts tab is.
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/imported", validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await profileImported(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/followers", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await followers(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/following", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await following(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );

  r.post("/profiles/:handle/follow", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setFollow(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, true)));
  r.delete("/profiles/:handle/follow", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setFollow(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, false)));
  r.post("/profiles/:handle/block", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setBlock(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, true)));
  r.delete("/profiles/:handle/block", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setBlock(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, false)));
  r.post("/profiles/:handle/mute", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setMute(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, true)));
  r.delete("/profiles/:handle/mute", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setMute(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, false)));

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the viewer's private lists

  r.get("/me/likes", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await likedPosts(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/me/bookmarks", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await bookmarkedPosts(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/me/blocks", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await blockedList(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/me/mutes", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await mutedList(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the viewer's own profile

  r.patch("/me/profile", guard, validate("json", ProfileEditRequest), async (c) => c.json({ profile: await editProfile(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("json")) }));
  r.post("/me/handle", guard, fresh, validate("json", HandleChangeRequest), async (c) => c.json({ profile: await changeHandle(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("json")) }));
  // "Show my posts in Explore": on and off, with no body, as the app's other switches.
  r.post("/me/explore", guard, async (c) => c.json(await setShowInExplore(deps, me(c), true)));
  r.delete("/me/explore", guard, async (c) => c.json(await setShowInExplore(deps, me(c), false)));
  // 2d (decision 21, 9.2): link previews of the account's posts and profile, on and off, written as the Explore switch.
  r.post("/me/share-previews", guard, async (c) => c.json(await setSharePreviews(deps, me(c), true)));
  r.delete("/me/share-previews", guard, async (c) => c.json(await setSharePreviews(deps, me(c), false)));

  return r;
}

/**
 * 3f (design, sections 5 and 7.12): GET /api/posts/:id/status, the one question Caddy asks the API for every request of a
 * post's page, so that a status check from outside reads what a person sees. A router of its own, mounted after the
 * global limit and before the session's resolution, as the image files' router is: Caddy's question carries the
 * visitor's cookies, and a route among the module's others would read a session for every page view. It parses the id
 * itself, since the validator would answer a malformed one with a JSON body, and answers 204 exactly when a post with
 * this id is visible, and 404 with no body otherwise (no such post, a malformed id, deleted by its author, withheld,
 * removed or disabled): the same for everyone, so it tells nothing a signed-out read of the post does not, and never 451.
 * No interface carries it: nothing outside this module calls it.
 */
export function postStatusRoutes(deps: Pick<SocialDeps, "repo">) {
  const r = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  r.get("/posts/:id/status", async (c) => {
    const id = PostId.safeParse(c.req.param("id"));
    if (!id.success) return c.body(null, 404);
    const row = (await deps.repo.findPosts([id.data])).get(id.data);
    return c.body(null, row?.state === "visible" ? 204 : 404);
  });
  return r;
}
```

```ts
import { IMPORT_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";

/**
 * Write limits by account age (2a spec, section 6). Sub-project 3 replaces the age check with
 * reputation without changing the buckets or the enforcement.
 */
export const HOUR_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;
export const DAY_MS = 24 * HOUR_MS;

/** Accounts younger than this get the low tier. */
export const NEW_ACCOUNT_MS = 24 * HOUR_MS;
/** Reposting and quoting need an account at least this old. */
export const REPOST_MIN_AGE_MS = 48 * HOUR_MS;

/** 3b (design, section 7.6): an import's chunks, its acts (cancel; confirm, stop and undo in later tasks) and its picks. */
export type ImportAction = "import-chunk" | "import-act" | "import-pick";
/**
 * 2d (design, section 9.5): the seen marker and the settings of Activity (the activity module counts them through this
 * module's index), the avatar's set and remove together (Task 3's routes), the link-preview switch and a post's hidden
 * counts.
 */
export type EngagementAction = "activity-seen" | "activity-settings" | "avatar" | "share-previews" | "hide-counts";
export type WriteAction = "post" | "reply" | "quote" | "repost" | "like" | "bookmark" | "follow" | "block" | "mute" | "upload" | ImportAction | EngagementAction;

export interface WriteLimit {
  /** Counter name; several actions may share one (quotes count as posts). */
  bucket: string;
  max: number;
  windowMs: number;
}

export const isNewAccount = (accountAgeMs: number): boolean => accountAgeMs < NEW_ACCOUNT_MS;
export const mayRepostOrQuote = (accountAgeMs: number): boolean => accountAgeMs >= REPOST_MIN_AGE_MS;

/** Every window an action must stay within. Follows have an hourly and a daily one. */
export function limitsFor(action: WriteAction, accountAgeMs: number): WriteLimit[] {
  const fresh = isNewAccount(accountAgeMs);
  switch (action) {
    case "post":
    case "quote":
      return [{ bucket: "post", max: fresh ? 5 : 30, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "reply":
      return [{ bucket: "reply", max: fresh ? 20 : 60, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "repost":
      return [{ bucket: "repost", max: 30, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "like":
      return [{ bucket: "like", max: 100, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "bookmark":
      return [{ bucket: "bookmark", max: 100, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "follow":
      return [
        { bucket: "follow-hour", max: 50, windowMs: HOUR_MS },
        { bucket: "follow-day", max: 400, windowMs: DAY_MS },
      ];
    case "block":
      return [{ bucket: "block", max: 30, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "mute":
      return [{ bucket: "mute", max: 30, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    // Image uploads (2b). The media module counts them through this table, so every per-account limit lives here.
    case "upload":
      return [
        { bucket: "upload", max: fresh ? 20 : 120, windowMs: HOUR_MS },
        { bucket: "upload-day", max: fresh ? 60 : 500, windowMs: DAY_MS },
      ];
    // 3b (design, section 7.6): the imports module counts these through this table too, at any age (an import needs an
    // account of seven days anyway). A 2 GiB archive is 256 chunks; 600 an hour leave room for retries.
    case "import-chunk":
      return [{ bucket: "import-chunk", max: IMPORT_RULES.chunksPerHour, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "import-act":
      return [{ bucket: "import-act", max: IMPORT_RULES.actsPerHour, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "import-pick":
      return [{ bucket: "import-pick", max: IMPORT_RULES.picksPerHour, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    // 2d (design, section 9.5): at any age. The marker moves once a visit, and the app saves a settled choice only (10.8).
    case "activity-seen":
      return [{ bucket: "activity-seen", max: 240, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "activity-settings":
      return [{ bucket: "activity-settings", max: 120, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "avatar":
      return [
        { bucket: "avatar-hour", max: 10, windowMs: HOUR_MS },
        { bucket: "avatar-day", max: 30, windowMs: DAY_MS },
      ];
    case "share-previews":
      return [{ bucket: "share-previews", max: 30, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
    case "hide-counts":
      return [{ bucket: "hide-counts", max: 60, windowMs: HOUR_MS }];
  }
}
```

```ts
import type { Author, HiddenMedia, MediaView, PostCounts, PostView, TimelineItem, Tombstone } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { PostImage } from "../media";
import type { SocialDeps, ViewerId } from "./context";
import { encodeCursor } from "./cursor";
import type { ListRow, PostRow, ProfileRow } from "./repo";
import { postAccess, tombstone } from "./visibility";

/** Where views come from: the posts, their images through the media module, and the chip's facts through the moderation module. */
export type ViewSource = Pick<SocialDeps, "repo" | "media" | "moderation">;

/** What a post id resolves to for a viewer: the view, or a tombstone when the viewer may not see it. */
export type LoadedPost = PostView | Tombstone;

export function isTombstone(loaded: LoadedPost): loaded is Tombstone {
  return !("author" in loaded);
}

export function authorOf(profile: ProfileRow): Author {
  return { id: profile.id, handle: profile.handle, displayName: profile.displayName, verified: profile.verified };
}

/**
 * One image of a post as this viewer gets it (3c design, section 7.10). A visible image is the image. A withheld or
 * removed one stays with its author, who gets it with that state; anyone else gets a placeholder in its place, the same
 * for both states, with nothing of the image in it. A sealed image is that placeholder for every viewer, its author
 * included, who alone is told that it is sealed.
 */
export function mediaFor(viewer: ViewerId, authorId: string, image: PostImage): MediaView | HiddenMedia {
  const own = viewer !== null && viewer === authorId;
  if (image.state === "sealed") return own ? { id: image.id, hidden: true, sealed: true } : { id: image.id, hidden: true };
  const { state, ...view } = image;
  if (state === "visible") return view;
  return own ? { ...view, moderation: state } : { id: image.id, hidden: true };
}

/**
 * 2d (decision 26, 9.3): a post's counts as this reader gets them, the one rule for every answer that carries counts (a
 * view, a quoted embed, and the engagement answer of flows/engagement.ts): likes and reposts are null exactly when the
 * author hid them and the reader is not the author; replies and quotes are always numbers. So nobody but the author
 * learns a hidden count, by reading it or by liking and unliking.
 */
export function countsFor(viewer: ViewerId, row: PostRow): PostCounts {
  const hidden = row.hideCounts && viewer !== row.authorId;
  return { likes: hidden ? null : row.likeCount, reposts: hidden ? null : row.repostCount, replies: row.replyCount, quotes: row.quoteCount };
}

/**
 * Turns post ids into views for one viewer: loads the rows and, one level deep, the posts they
 * quote; decides access for every row with the visibility rule and the viewer's blocks; attaches
 * the viewer's like, repost and bookmark state, and every post's images, each as this viewer gets it
 * (mediaFor). Ids that resolve to nothing become tombstones, and tombstones carry no images. The
 * viewer's own visible posts that the current Explore ranking holds, while their switch is on, carry
 * the author's chip (2c design, section 8):
 * asked in one query, and only when the viewer wrote some of the posts; a quoted embed never carries it.
 * The viewer's own withheld and removed posts carry the decision behind their state (3c design, section 7.6), which the
 * moderation module names: asked the same way, once for the page and only when the viewer wrote such a post.
 * 2d (4.3): each post it shows carries the mentions that link for this viewer, read for the page's shown posts in one
 * statement (mentionsFor); a quoted embed carries none. Counts go through countsFor.
 */
export async function loadPostViews({ repo, media, moderation }: ViewSource, viewer: ViewerId, ids: string[]): Promise<Map<string, LoadedPost>> {
  const unique = [...new Set(ids)];
  const primary = await repo.findPosts(unique);
  const quoteIds = [...new Set([...primary.values()].map((row) => row.quoteOfId).filter((id): id is string => id !== null && !primary.has(id)))];
  const quoted = await repo.findPosts(quoteIds);
  const all = new Map([...primary, ...quoted]);
  const authorIds = [...new Set([...all.values()].flatMap((row) => (row.replyToAuthorId ? [row.authorId, row.replyToAuthorId] : [row.authorId])))];
  const blocked = viewer ? await repo.blockedEitherWay(viewer, authorIds) : new Set<string>();
  const states = viewer ? await repo.viewerPostStates(viewer, [...all.keys()]) : null;
  const images = await media.forPosts([...all.keys()]);
  // A withheld or removed post is never in Explore for anyone, its author included, so only visible ones are asked about.
  // Whether the author is suspended when this reads is listedInExplore's to judge (3e), so the chip goes with the page.
  const own = viewer ? [...primary.values()].filter((row) => row.authorId === viewer && row.state === "visible").map((row) => row.id) : [];
  const inExplore = viewer && own.length > 0 ? await repo.listedInExplore(viewer, own) : new Set<string>();
  // The chip of a withheld or removed post is its author's alone, so only the viewer's own such posts are asked about.
  const restricted = viewer ? [...primary.values()].filter((row) => row.authorId === viewer && (row.state === "withheld" || row.state === "removed")).map((row) => row.id) : [];
  const decisions = viewer && moderation && restricted.length > 0 ? await moderation.authorFacts(viewer, restricted) : null;

  const access = (row: PostRow) => postAccess(viewer, row, blocked.has(row.authorId));
  // Only the posts this viewer is shown: a hidden or deleted post's mentions are never read.
  const mentioned = await repo.mentionsFor(viewer, [...primary.values()].filter((row) => access(row) === "shown").map((row) => row.id));
  /** The parent's handle only when the viewer could open the parent; a block either way, or a hidden or deleted parent, gives null. */
  const parentHandle = (row: PostRow): string | null =>
    row.replyToAuthorId && row.replyToState && postAccess(viewer, { authorId: row.replyToAuthorId, state: row.replyToState }, blocked.has(row.replyToAuthorId)) === "shown"
      ? row.replyToHandle
      : null;
  const base = (row: PostRow) => ({
    id: row.id,
    author: row.author,
    body: row.body,
    createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString(),
    state: row.state as PostView["state"],
    replyTo: row.replyToId ? { id: row.replyToId, authorHandle: parentHandle(row) } : null,
    counts: countsFor(viewer, row),
    media: (images.get(row.id) ?? []).map((image) => mediaFor(viewer, row.authorId, image)),
    ...(states ? { viewer: states.get(row.id)! } : {}),
  });
  const quoteOf = (id: string | null): PostView["quoteOf"] => {
    if (id === null) return null;
    const row = all.get(id);
    if (!row) return tombstone(id, "hidden");
    const a = access(row);
    // 3b: a quoted post carries its provenance label too, last, for the embed's short line (10.6).
    return a === "shown" ? { ...base(row), quoteOf: null, imported: row.imported } : tombstone(id, a);
  };

  const out = new Map<string, LoadedPost>();
  for (const id of unique) {
    const row = primary.get(id);
    if (!row) {
      out.set(id, tombstone(id, "hidden"));
      continue;
    }
    const a = access(row);
    const decision = decisions?.get(id);
    // 3b (9.3): the provenance label, from the post's own columns: the archive's day, never its second. 2d (9.3): then the
    // mentions that link for this viewer and the author's hidden-counts switch, last.
    out.set(
      id,
      a === "shown"
        ? {
            ...base(row),
            ...(inExplore.has(id) ? { inExplore: true as const } : {}),
            ...(decision ? { moderation: decision } : {}),
            quoteOf: quoteOf(row.quoteOfId),
            imported: row.imported,
            mentions: mentioned.get(id) ?? [],
            countsHidden: row.hideCounts,
          }
        : tombstone(id, a),
    );
  }
  return out;
}

/** One post as the viewer sees it, or null when they may not. */
export async function postView(source: ViewSource, viewer: ViewerId, id: string): Promise<PostView | null> {
  const loaded = (await loadPostViews(source, viewer, [id])).get(id)!;
  return isTombstone(loaded) ? null : loaded;
}

/** Views for list rows, in list order, dropping anything the viewer may not see. */
export async function postViews(source: ViewSource, viewer: ViewerId, rows: ListRow[]): Promise<PostView[]> {
  const loaded = await loadPostViews(source, viewer, rows.map((row) => row.postId));
  return rows.map((row) => loaded.get(row.postId)!).filter((view): view is PostView => !isTombstone(view));
}

/** Timeline items for list rows, with the reposter attached to repost rows. */
export async function timelineItems(source: ViewSource, viewer: ViewerId, rows: ListRow[]): Promise<TimelineItem[]> {
  const loaded = await loadPostViews(source, viewer, rows.map((row) => row.postId));
  const reposters = await source.repo.findProfiles([...new Set(rows.map((row) => row.reposterId).filter((id): id is string => id !== null))]);
  const items: TimelineItem[] = [];
  for (const row of rows) {
    const view = loaded.get(row.postId)!;
    if (isTombstone(view)) continue;
    const reposter = row.reposterId ? reposters.get(row.reposterId) : undefined;
    if (row.reposterId && !reposter) continue;
    items.push(reposter ? { kind: "repost", post: view, repostedBy: authorOf(reposter), repostedAt: row.sortAt.toISOString() } : { kind: "post", post: view });
  }
  return items;
}

/** The cursor for the page after these rows, or null when the page was not full. */
export function pageCursor(rows: { sortAt: Date; postId?: string; profileId?: string; reposterId?: string | null }[], limit: number): string | null {
  if (rows.length < limit) return null;
  const last = rows[rows.length - 1]!;
  return encodeCursor({ t: last.sortAt.getTime(), id: (last.postId ?? last.profileId)!, ...(last.reposterId ? { r: last.reposterId } : {}) });
}
```

```tsx
import { fullDate, postedWhen, timeAgo } from "@/lib/time";

/**
 * A link inside a line of text (the author line, the repost line, the reply context): inline, so a phone holds it to

const INLINE_LINK = cn("rounded-sm py-1.5 web:hover:underline", FOCUS_RING);

/**
 * Who wrote the post and when (UI design, section 6.6): the display name in body-strong as the link to the profile, the
 * verified chip, the handle in the mono face, and the time as the post's one link. The time shows its short form ("3h"),
 * hidden from the link's name, which says it inside postedWhen's words ("3h ago, open the post"), so the name contains
 * the visible label. The thread's focused post shows the full date instead. The card's own line marks its time link as
 * the article's open link (`open`), which a feed's Page Down and Page Up move the focus to; a quote's line does not.
 */
function AuthorLine({ author, createdAt, postId, large = false, open = false }: { author: Author; createdAt: string; postId: string; large?: boolean; open?: boolean }) {
  const shown = large ? fullDate(createdAt) : timeAgo(createdAt);
  const when = large ? fill(UI_WORDS["time.posted.on"], { date: shown }) : postedWhen(createdAt);
  return (
    <View className="flex-row flex-wrap items-center gap-x-1.5">
      <Text variant="body-strong">
        <Link href={`/u/${author.handle}`} asChild>

        </Link>
      </Text>
      {author.verified ? <VerifiedChip /> : null}
      <Text variant="mono" tone="low">

      <Text variant="meta" tone="low">
        <Link href={`/post/${postId}`} asChild>
          <Inline {...(open ? dataAttribute("open") : {})} className={cn(INLINE_LINK, "px-1.5")}>
            <Inline aria-hidden>{shown}</Inline>

}

/** The repost line above a reposted post: the repost icon, and "Ben reposted" with Ben's name a link to his profile. */

 * from the post's own label alone. It is a 44 px button that opens Who sees this at its provenance paragraph, named with
 * the day written out and what it opens ("... dated 3 March 2019. About imported posts"). The day is the archive's, in UTC.
 */
function ImportedLine({ label, onPress }: { label: ImportedLabel; onPress: () => void }) {

  return (
    <Pressable

        {words.text}
      </Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}

/** A quoted post that is gone: its sentence in the text face's italic, on surface-2 (section 8.3). */
function TombstoneBox({ tombstone }: { tombstone: Tombstone }) {
  return (
    <View className="mt-2 rounded-media bg-surface-2 px-3 py-2.5">
      <Text tone="medium" italic>
        {tombstone.deleted ? UI_WORDS["post.deleted"] : UI_WORDS["post.unavailable"]}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}

/** What a press on a card's empty space must leave alone: its links and controls, which act for themselves. */
const CONTROL = "a, button, input, textarea, select, [role=button], [role=link], [role=dialog], [role=switch]";

/**
 * The open target of a card's body for pointers on the web (section 6.6): a click on the card that is not on one of its
 * links or controls, and that does not end a text selection, opens `href`. A click from a menu or sheet the card opened
 * reaches this handler through React's portal, but is not inside the card's own element, so it is left alone.
 */
function opensOnClick(open: () => void) {
  return (event: MouseEvent & { currentTarget: Element; target: Element }) => {
    const root = event.currentTarget;
    if (!root.contains(event.target)) return;
    const control = event.target.closest?.(CONTROL);
    if (control && root.contains(control)) return;
    const selection = typeof window !== "undefined" ? window.getSelection() : null;
    if (selection && !selection.isCollapsed && selection.anchorNode && root.contains(selection.anchorNode)) return;
    event.stopPropagation();
    open();
  };
}

/**
 * The quoted post as the composer previews it (UI design, Task 6): the same frame and words, with its author line as
 * text, nothing to open and nothing to click, so the composer's sheet holds no live link out of the post being written.
 */
function QuotePreview({ quote }: { quote: QuotedPost }) {
  return (
    <View className="mt-2 rounded-media border border-line-low px-3 py-2.5">
      <View className="flex-row flex-wrap items-center gap-x-1.5">
        <Text variant="body-strong">{quote.author.displayName}</Text>
        {quote.author.verified ? <VerifiedChip /> : null}
        <Text variant="mono" tone="low">
          @{quote.author.handle}
        </Text>
        <Text variant="meta" tone="low">
          {timeAgo(quote.createdAt)}
        </Text>
      </View>
      {/* 3b (10.6): the short label of a quoted imported post, here as in QuoteEmbed. */}
      {quote.imported ? (
        <Text variant="meta" tone="medium">
          {importedShort(quote.imported.source)}
        </Text>
      ) : null}
      {quote.body ? <Text className="mt-0.5">{quote.body}</Text> : null}
      <MediaGrid media={quote.media} compact />
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * A quoted post (section 6.6): a bordered region with its own author line, whose time is the link to the quoted post,
 * so the quote has one open target too; its words are plain text, and its images open nothing, since they belong to the
 * quoted post, where the grid and the viewer are. A press on its empty space opens the quoted post. `preview` is the
 * composer's form, which opens nothing (QuotePreview).
 */
export function QuoteEmbed({ quote, preview = false }: { quote: QuotedPost | Tombstone; preview?: boolean }) {
  if (!("author" in quote)) return <TombstoneBox tombstone={quote} />;
  if (preview) return <QuotePreview quote={quote} />;
  const open = () => router.push(`/post/${quote.id}`);
  const content = (
    <>
      <AuthorLine author={quote.author} createdAt={quote.createdAt} postId={quote.id} />
      {/* 3b (10.6): a quoted imported post shows the label's short form, as text. */}
      {quote.imported ? (
        <Text variant="meta" tone="medium">
          {importedShort(quote.imported.source)}
        </Text>
      ) : null}
      {quote.body ? <Text className="mt-0.5">{quote.body}</Text> : null}
      <MediaGrid media={quote.media} compact postId={quote.id} />
    </>
  );
  if (Platform.OS !== "web") {
    return (
      <Pressable accessible={false} {...pressDelay(80)} onPress={open} className="mt-2 rounded-media border border-line-low px-3 py-2.5 active:bg-surface-2">
        {content}
      </Pressable>
    );
  }
  return (
    <View {...({ onClick: opensOnClick(open) } as object)} className="mt-2 rounded-media border border-line-low px-3 py-2.5 web:cursor-pointer web:hover:bg-surface-2 web:transition-colors web:duration-[120ms]">
      {content}
    </View>
  );

/**
 * The chip on the author's own withheld or removed post (3c design, section 9; UI design, sections 4.8, 6.13 and 8.7).
 * With the decision behind the state it names the rule or says "illegal content", in the review tone while korbat decides
 * and the restricted tone once removed, and is the button that opens StatusSheet, the decision's details, named by its
 * own words; the sheet is mounted only while it is open, and the focus comes back to the chip when it has closed. Its
 * state lives here, in the card, so opening it redraws no row of the list. A view without the decision's facts still
 * says the state, as information only.
```
